<!-- What is established about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as it stands now, grouped by area: each entry the fact, its source and its test. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `FACTS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before. What an entry holds and how it is written: the `coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`. -->

# Facts on record

## Execution model

- F-7 **Walk and the compiled path share the parser and the phases, and only the compiled path runs the static type checker.** Walk switches the checker off, and no switch turns it on. So walk checks no static types of expressions: an ill-typed expression shows only when it runs, as a failed dispatch or as another run-time error, such as F-239's refusal of an `if` on a value that is not a `Boolean`. At load, walk refuses some ill-formed declarations: the `fortress-repo` skill's `interpreter.md`, "What walk checks", lists them, with their evidence in F-29 (`comprises` clauses), F-142 (the Meet Rule for Functional Methods) and F-145 (uncovered abstract methods and `override`). The phases and where the two paths part: the skill's "How a program runs". Detail: `explorations/repo-internals.md`, "The two worlds".
- F-9 **`fortress typecheck` checks a program against the compiler's library, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, so it is no oracle for walk programs.** `Shell.java` calls `useCompilerLibraries()` for the command (row 69). P-12 has walk run the checker on its own programs after the switch-over, and walk cannot do so as it stands: it runs with type checking and the Scala checker off, the Java checker is gone (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:228-229`), and it has no case for the `CoercionInvocation` nodes that the checker inserts, by reading (row 833).
- F-11 **The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main representational cost of microGPT-shaped array code.** So a compiled `RR64` loop holds no `dadd` or `dmul` (the `fortress-repo` skill, "The compiled runtime"). In Java models of microGPT's three kernels, boxed elements cost 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`. No such kernel compiles yet: the compiler prelude has no array type (row 305), and the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (P-37). In a hot compiled loop, escape analysis removes the temporary boxes, and one box per assignment to a mutable variable per iteration stays (F-301), as long as C2's inline depth reaches each box's constructor chain (F-302). Detail: `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 4; `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` section 4.
- F-12 **On the compiled path, the scalar `RR64` loop `bench1t` ran in 0.74 s in one session's measurement; the loop still pays for its generator, for boxing and for a transaction check at each use of its accumulator.** `bench1t` is `for i <- seq(1#20000000) do acc := acc 0.9999999 + 0.0000001 end` on a `var acc: RR64`, with both literals written in the loop. The time is the median of three loop-only runs at one thread (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`, "The four timings"). Times taken in different sessions differ on this machine, so compare only times from one session. What the loop does, read in its bytecode (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 5): the `seq` loop becomes the compiler prelude's `countedseqloop`, which runs the iterations in order by a recursive split over boxed indices, with a closure call per element; each value is boxed (F-11); and the accumulator is a volatile cell whose read and write each first call `BaseTask.inATransaction`, as for every mutable local (F-40, what a size costs at run time, whose sized loop pays the same check). Within the boxing and the cell, the report counts four allocations per iteration, an interface call to the native wrapper and the casts, the part that unboxed doubles and `double[]` would attack. No share of the 0.74 s is measured.
- F-17 **The bytecode cache can come up empty after a library order that reports exit 0.** Running the same commands again, one at a time, made the jars. The cause is not known. Check the five jars before a compiled run (the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md`, "The library order"). Detail: `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-18 **On the compiled path, the class loader makes the class of a generic instantiation at its first use, by rewriting the template's bytecode with ASM, and the rewriting only renames, so it gives no instance a `double[]` field.** The class is `InstantiatingClassloader`; the `fortress-repo` skill's "The compiled runtime" gives the mechanism. A size is part of the made class's name, as in `pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, the object `Box` at size 3 in the probe component `pNatMeth`. Inside the class, the size's descriptor is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` (F-129). A field of the template's type `T`, `LT;`, becomes `LFRR64;` in `Box⟦FRR64⟧`, and `[D` is no class name, so stamping alone keeps every number boxed (F-11). The team's direction for unboxing builds on this class per instantiation (the plan in `compiler/optimization/Unbox.java`; the loader's empty "expando" stub, `runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:168-172`), but a loader that stamps an `RR64` instance with a `double[]` field, way A4 of array decision A (P-85), does not exist and is unmeasured. Walk instantiates generics in its own evaluator, not by classes. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` section 1; `coordinator/array-design.md` section 2 (probe 1); `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 3, way A4.
- F-19 **By the specification, the iterations of a `for` loop, the elements of a tuple, and the arguments of a call or an operator may run in parallel, and a program must assume that they do.** A `for` loop is sequential only if every generator is, as `seq(g)` or `sequential(g)` makes it. An implementation may also run them one after another (`evaluation/parallelism.tex:88-90`), so a program cannot count on parallel runs either. For the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator, each path starts a task only where it judges it worth it: walk by `TupleTask.worthSpawning`, which also governs a call's arguments, and the code generator by `ParallelismAnalyzer`. Compiled, a function call's arguments run in order (`CodeGen.evalArg`). A `for` loop over a range without `seq` runs by splitting the range into `do … also do … end` blocks. Under walk, every such block is a task, and walk's library splits down to single elements (`Library/RangeInternals.fss`). Compiled, the first block runs in place, and each other block forks only where `BaseTask.forkIfProfitable` judges it worth it, as tuple elements do; the compiler prelude's `parloop` splits down to `FORTRESS_LOOP_CHUNK` elements, 1 by default. `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the pool of worker threads (the `fortress-repo` skill, "Parallelism and mutable state"). By grep, no program under `explorations/`, the model programs and the probes, writes `spawn`, which starts an explicit thread, or an `also do` block, so their parallelism comes only from loops, tuples and arguments. The revival's tests under `ProjectFortress/` write both. Source: `Specification/basic/expressions/for.tex:28-32`, `tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:58-59`, `evaluation/parallelism.tex:50-80`.
- F-20 **Sizes, the `nat` and `int` static parameters, are values at run time; they check shapes, and no optimization uses them (F-40, what a size costs at run time).** The compiled checker checks them (F-67), and a sized program loads and runs compiled (F-129). Under walk, `Vector` and `Matrix` take their sizes from an array built at run time: `f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\])` takes `s` from `array[\RR64\](3)`, and overloads on `Vector` and `Matrix` dispatch by rank (row 214). The array-type syntax `T[n]` with a `nat` parameter does not unify with such an array, "Cannot unify … with ArrayType", where `T[3]` with a literal size does (row 23). Walk matches sizes at dispatch. A mismatch, such as a `DOT`, the library's inner product, of a 2×3 matrix by a 2×3 matrix, whose inner sizes differ, is a `ProgramError`, "Failed to find any matching overload", that no `catch` takes (row 254). Source: `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:96`.
- F-21 **The February 2011 Working Draft's bare `Nothing`, one object for every `T`, is accepted on neither path: the grammar refuses its `excludes` clause, and without that clause `T` is undefined.** The declaration is `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/convenience.tex:40`). Both paths stop at a syntax error at `excludes`, since an object has no `excludes` clause (measured: `reviews/spec-refused-examples.md`, E4). Without that clause, both report `T is undefined` at the `T` of the `extends` clause: a `where` clause on an object binds no type variable of its `extends` clause, as row 17 holds for a trait. Today's specification refuses the form in any case, by instantiation exclusion, and marks it "Not allowed" beside the parametric `Nothing[\T\]` that the interpreter's library writes (F-167). P-90 still calls the bare `Nothing` future work that waits for such `where` clauses, not tried before then. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-maybe/REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-22 **When a component's name differs from the api that it exports, neither path finds the component, for an exported function or variable alike.** The specification resolves an imported api to any component that exports it (`Specification/basic/components/overview.tex`). The tree looks only under the api's name, unless a user maps the api to its component by hand with `LinkShell`'s `alink` or `clink`. The linker's component repository looks this way (`Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`), so `fortress link` and walk print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path" before any code is generated. The code generator names a reference to an exported declaration after the api, and the declaring class after the component. The link step rewrites such a reference to the component only when the repository names it, so files compiled one by one, without `fortress link`, die with `NoClassDefFoundError`. The missing step is the repository's: finding the component that exports the api. The report names two repairs, neither built: the repository could search the source path for that component, or the code generator could emit api-named forwarders, for which three comments in `CodeGen.java` leave a place. Walk and `fortress link` need the first. Workaround: name the api after its component. Gated by the expected failure `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test` (row 320). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-export-var/REPORT.md`, "The measurement that separates them".
- F-23 **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it.** The parser's `createSpan` trims back over spaces only, and a declaration that ends in `end` is unaffected (row 359). So a comment-only library edit can change the syntax tree, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics maps positions back first. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md` section 6, D1.
- F-24 **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees.** It throws a `FortressError` that holds the exception's object, as `Int.overflow()` does for `IntegerOverflow` (F-132; row 347, fixed). A native bound to a helper of `nativeHelpers/` raises the library's own exception where the helper raises a class of the compiled prelude, such as `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$DivisionByZero`, so `DIV`, `REM` and `MOD` by zero on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `NN32` and `NN64` raise `DivisionByZero` (F-299, F-306, F-308, F-312). Any other Java exception of a native becomes a `ProgramError`, which no `catch` takes. Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`, and for a helper by `tests/NativeHelperRaiseWalk.fss` and, for each of the five types, `tests/<type>DivisionByZeroWalk.fss` and `tests/<type>RemainderByZeroWalk.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md` section 4.1.
- F-25 **On the compiled path, the class loader loads each class under the JDK's class-loading lock, so the first load of an instantiation's class is safe on four threads at once.** `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` holds `getClassLoadingLock(name)` for the whole load, as the JDK's own `ClassLoader.loadClass` does. Without the lock, two threads that first loaded such classes at the same time could race, and the run died with a `NullPointerException` (row 417, fixed). The test `compiler_tests/FirstLoadThreadsRungG` calls the generic overload `f[\T\](v: Vt[\T\])` at eight instantiations, `Vt[\A1\]` to `Vt[\A8\]`, from a parallel `for` loop of 800 iterations. Observed: at four threads it failed 5 runs of 5 before the lock, and passed 5 of 5 after. It is one of the gate's atomic runs, which run each program at four threads (`gate.md`). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 (the runs) and 12 (why this lock).
- F-26 **Under walk, when one of two applicable declarations has static parameters of its own, the call chooses on their declared domains where exactly one lies inside the other, not by the order in which they are written.** It builds P-45, the choice among overloads by declared parameter types, under walk. A declaration has static parameters of its own if it is a generic function or constructor, or a functional method with static parameters in a trait or object without any. Its declared domain, walk's symbolic instance, is its parameter types with each type parameter standing for itself under its bounds. Where neither declared domain lies inside the other, where each lies inside the other, or where neither declaration has static parameters of its own, walk compares the domains of the instances that the call makes. So a functional method of a generic trait or object is compared on its instance, and a generic dotted method is chosen by F-253 (a generic method at a dotted call, also chosen on declared domains). If the chosen declaration is generic and its instance takes an argument only by a conversion, walk converts the argument and dispatches the converted arguments again, so the most specific declaration for the converted values runs. In two cases walk keeps the chosen instance, with no second dispatch: an overloaded dotted method, and a position whose conversion `Coercions.coercionFor` does not find, such as a tuple converted element by element. Two generic overloads whose static parameters agree in name, kind and bounds share one symbolic instance, even if their `where` clauses differ; no test or library declaration has such a pair (row 478). Gated by `tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss` and `DispatchConvertedAgain.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.1, 5.2 (the second dispatch) and 5.5 (the symbolic instance).
- F-27 **Walk's load check reads again two kinds of overload pair that its parameter-by-parameter check refuses, and accepts those that pass: a generic declaration beside a plain one, read on their declared domains, and two plain top-level functions, not methods, whose overlap other declarations cover through `comprises` clauses.** To test a cover, the check cuts the overlap of the two domains, position by position, into parts by the `comprises` clauses. Each combination of parts must lie inside the domain of one declaration without static parameters that lies below both. So several such declarations may together cover the overlap. A search that does not settle refuses. A generic declaration beside a plain one passes where one declared domain lies strictly inside the other and the inner one's return type lies below the outer one's. Where neither lies inside the other, the pair needs the same cover, or declared domains that exclude each other read whole (F-258, exclusion over the whole parameter type). Equal declared domains are refused. It builds under walk P-46, by which a conversion never changes which declaration runs when one already fits, and P-60, by which several declarations below both may cover a meet. Two generic declarations are read on their declared domains too (F-252: the No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet Rules, each over its own instances). Walk still refuses the valid example of the POPL 2019 paper on symmetric multiple dispatch (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`, p. 11:13), a set of three generic declarations (row 539). Gated by `tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss` and `GenericBesidePlain*.fss`, among others. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.3 (generic beside plain) and 5.4 (the cover).
- F-28 **Walk instantiates a generic declaration declared to return `Any`.** `MakeInferenceSpecific` treats `Any` as it treats a trait type (row 157, fixed). Its visitor has no case for 11 of the syntax tree's 18 concrete type classes, and of those only the dimension forms can be written as a return type. Gated by `tests/GenericReturningAny.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 3.
- F-29 **Under walk, the load check refuses a trait or object that extends a closed trait of the program's main component where the trait's `comprises` clause does not allow it.** A closed trait is one with a `comprises` clause. The check reads every trait and object of every component of the program, the library's included, as a possible extender. An extender is allowed in three cases: it lies below a listed type; it is a trait whose own `comprises` clause lists only types that are allowed in turn; or it is a generic trait that some trait or object extends, and each of those extenders lies below a listed type (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations"). The check does not yet read a clause declared outside the main component, the library's among them (row 551), or an object expression's `extends` clause (row 597). Nor does it check that each listed type extends the trait at every instantiation (row 598). A check that read the library's clauses would refuse at load every program that imports the library's `Reflect` (row 595), and four team tests and two demos whose objects extend `Number` or `Exception` directly (row 596). Their repairs come before that check and are the curator's. Gated by `tests/ComprisesUnlistedExtender` and `ComprisesGenericChildUnlistedExtender`, refused at load, and by the `XXX` tests of rows 487 (a type of another component below a generic subtrait of a closed trait), 551, 597 and 598, which stay green while walk still loads their programs. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-load-check/REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-269 **Under walk, a program's declarations of a library operator name are checked against the library's only when the program declares two or more of that name, and only on a cold cache.** One such declaration is not checked. Two or more are checked with the library's declarations, and the check can refuse them beside the library's generic declarations, even where they are more specific than the library's. It refused C4's former pair of `MAX` between an `RR64` and an `Array[\RR64,I\]`, in both orders, which C4 dropped when F-119's scalar extension took its place (row 341). It refuses the `Matrix`-specialised elementwise `×` of `apl/mg/elemwise_nat_probe.fss` (F-155). Walk writes a component to its cache before it runs this check, and skips the check on a component that it reads back. So a refusal appears once, on a cold cache, and never again (row 342). The check runs only when walk analyses the library itself again: deleting the program's own cache entries does not bring it back (row 342). So a test that depends on this check must run from an empty cache. Detail: rows 341 and 342; `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md` section 4, a gated run that met a warm cache.
- F-291 **With the bound `Any`, the compiled path compiles, loads and runs generics at tuple and arrow static arguments as it does with `extends Any` written; `()` fails whatever the bound (row 339), and so does a generic dotted method with one tuple-typed parameter (row 832).** Measured once: generic functions, objects and traits, dispatch to a generic arm and `typecase`, at a pair or an arrow, with the static argument written or inferred. The class loader made the same classes by name, and the program jars read the same under `javap`, as the same programs with `extends Any` written under the compile command's bound `Object`. So the switch to the bound `Any` costs the run time no work for these shapes; its test cost is F-292. Not run: the one library's own instantiations at tuples, tuples of three or more and nested ones, generic functional methods at a tuple, a native that receives a tuple. With `extends Object` written, they are refused, or pass unchecked where the static argument is written (row 470); the compile command's bound is `Any` (`Shell.java:372`). No gated test. Detail: `perf-probes/bound-any-compiled/REPORT.md`, "The shapes by setting" and "What the class loader makes".
- F-301 **On the compiled path a native helper is called through a generated wrapper over the box classes, and once the loop is hot C2 inlines the whole path, so the call costs nothing of its own.** A binding `builtinPrimitive("pkg.Class.method")` and a written `import java` alias call compile to the same bytes: an `invokestatic` of `native.pkg.Class.method`, a class the compiled path writes into `nativewrapper_cache/`, which unboxes each argument with `getValue`, calls the helper and boxes its result with `make`, a new box each time (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressMethodAdapter.java:303-327`; `compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32.java:22-24`). A functional method such as `ZZ32`'s `+` reaches the wrapper through the dispatcher, an interface call, the springboard and the trait's static body. C2 inlines all of these frames, the helper, `make` and the box's constructor chain; only C1's profiling code refuses the helper and the chain's deep frames. Escape analysis then removes every temporary box, a helper's result passed into another helper among them, and one box stays per assignment to a mutable variable per iteration: 16 bytes for a `ZZ32`, 24 for an `RR64`. The library's form and the prelude's allocate the same. Observed once on one small program, `perf-probes/helper-calls/HelperCalls.fss`, by `javap`, C2's inlining log and the bytes that JFR counted, with no timing, on a machine shared at a load of 20 to 25; no test checks it. Detail: `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` sections 2 to 5.
- F-302 **In those loops C2 inlines down to depth 12 from the loop, against the 16 at which it stops by default, and a temporary box whose constructor chain passes the limit is no longer removed.** At JDK 25's default `MaxInlineLevel=15` a frame at depth d inlines when d is at most 16. The prelude's `+` reaches `Object.<init>` under its result's box at depth 12, a top-level binding at 10. With the limit lowered to 8, a loop of two nested helper calls rose from 33 to 96 bytes per iteration, since its temporaries' chains no longer inlined. So an operator called from more than 4 further inlined frames keeps its temporary boxes. By reading, the one library's `ZZ32` springboard chain is two classes longer than the prelude's, `ZZ32`, `AnyIntegral`, `Number`, `AnyAdditiveGroup`, `Object`, `Any` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:730`, `:677`, `:380`, `:356`) against `ZZ32`, `Number`, `Object`, `Any` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:210`), since a springboard extends the springboard of its trait's first `extends` entry (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5072-5080`). If `FZZ32` extends the one library's springboard after the switch-over, the margin is 2 frames; not measured, since nothing compiles against the one library yet. Observed once (F-301). Detail: `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` sections 3 and 4.
## The checker and the one library

- F-32 **The compiled path cannot reuse walk's glue classes, the Java classes that 143 of the one library's 449 live native bindings still name.** A native binding is a library body `builtinPrimitive("…")`; its string names a glue class, which takes walk's boxed values, or a static helper of `nativeHelpers/`, over plain Java values, which both paths call (F-298; F-299 holds the 306 that name one). Matched against those helpers at `a1f8c4b8b`, before any binding moved, the 449 were: 154 whose operation the compiler's prelude already binds to a helper at the same owner and signature, so only the binding's string changes, to name that helper (P-58); 59 whose helper exists, but no binding names it under that name and signature, 23 of them under a name that the compiler's prelude gives to another helper, such as the 12 wrapping operators (row 348); 158 that need a new helper; and 78 that need more, 36 methods of native I/O objects and 42 with no compiled analogue. Of the 449, 29 are object `IntLiteral`'s (`FortressBuiltin.fss:486-563`), 4 among the 154 and 25 among the 158; none of them can move yet, since their helpers take and answer the compiled path's `IntLiteral`, which walk's values cannot be, and walk reaches no `IntLiteral` native while its numeral is an `Int` (P-76; row 578). Every program's output needs `Writer`'s natives, among the 36 I/O methods, since `println` writes through a native `Writer`. MicroGPT's `nanoTime` names a helper (F-314); it also needs `getProgramArgsPrim`, which `System` calls as it loads; and `NativeArray`. The last two have no compiled analogue. The 42 with no analogue: `NativeArray` waits for the array decision on how a float vector's `double[]` store goes (P-85), and `Thread`, `Reflect` and `printTaskTrace` are off microGPT's path. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` section 2; `coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-23.md`, section 4, "The planner's probes", "On the new base" and "The count".
- F-34 **Under the switch-over's setting the code generator refuses 38 declarations of the fourteen components that the distance stage checks, in 10 kinds, all of them declarations that the checker passes.** The setting is the distance stage's (F-53): the checker's failures caught per declaration, and the bound `Any`. Measured once, on `dbf4825e0`'s code, by `compile-ladder/plan-25/probes/codegen.sh` with its 288 helper strings put back on their glue classes; before local functions compiled, the same probe gave 47 in 11 kinds. The kinds that F-315 removes (`Any` in an `extends` clause, `forbid` and the `test` modifier) and the local function (F-320) no longer occur. A declaration counted at its first wall, and no emitted class was run. Each kind left has a ledger row or a plan line, among them varargs (row 624), `asif` (row 818) and "Not in the trait table" (row 733), so after the switch-over the code generator still stands between the library and bytecode. On climb batch 21b's base (`aa5c67d48`) the dispatch generator refused none of `FortressLibrary`'s 178 overload sets. No test checks the 38, since the gate's distance stage runs no code generation. 61	- F-64 **The compiled checker refuses every type that an api declares, trait or object, that extends a trait whose `comprises` clause has `...`, whether the clause lists it or not (row 354, open).** So the form `comprises { T, ... }` cannot stand in an api that declares `T`. The refusal runs only when the checker checks an api, so a component's types may extend such a trait. The specification's text allows `...` in an api's clause, and an extender that the clause lists (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations"). Only a draft note refuses the api's own declaration of an extender, and a release build leaves draft notes out. The team's `compiler_tests/XXX3q` and `XXX10p` pin the refusal, so a fix that skips it for a listed type turns them red. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-defects/REPORT.md`, "Defects and their homes".

By reading, both functions depend only on the table and the type. One differential on climb batch 7C's tree gave the same errors at the same sites with the memo off and on: 626 at the distance stage and 75 at the count stage. With the memo off, the count stage's 900-second limit stopped it; a copy with the limit raised took 1,149 s, against 112 s with the memo on. F-240 gives the stage's time today, with the memo on; its time with the memo off has not been measured since. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/REPORT.md`, "Why the memo changes no answer"; `reviews/row-488-probe.md`, "The answer".

Step 8 of a batch's gate compares it with the newest landed table. The total is never red on its own, as P-39 rules, since a fix can raise it and the effects of two rungs on it do not add up. The gate is red on a crash line that no rung declared in its manifest (`expectedCheckerCrash`), on a table with no total, and on a stale shadow: the instrumented copy of `StaticChecker` beside the stage (`checker-count/shadow-src/`), when the tracked `StaticChecker` no longer matches the checksum that `run.sh` records. Detail: `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "The checker count, and a rung whose test is that stage".

Two sizes are equal when their written forms are, once each operation on numerals is computed, so `2 3` equals `6` but `m n` does not equal `n m` (F-146). The checker refuses to infer a `bool`, `dim` or `unit` static argument (`XXXNatBoolChecker`). It does not compare `bool` arguments, so `object F extends { Flag[\true\], Flag[\false\] }`, two instantiations of one trait, passes it, and code generation then stops on it (row 406, open, a part of P-40 still to build). A call that leaves a size unknown is refused, "Could not infer static argument ... without context"; F-69 gives when an overload set is refused and when it is not. It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatInferredChecker`, `NatWrittenChecker`, `NatMethodChecker`, `NatExportChecker` and `XXXNatMismatchChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 1.

So an override returning `Dn[\T,3,s\]` over `Up[\T,b,s\]` is refused, like its type-parameter twin, and the library's `subarray` override passes. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatOverrideChecker` and `XXXNatRetSizeChecker`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/REPORT.md` section 5.

It drops instead an arm whose unknown size is in its own parameter types (row 400, open). It lets through a call whose argument's static type lies above the arm's domain, and the compiled run dies reading the size (row 446, open). It builds P-40. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatKnownSizeArm`, which compiles and runs a call that fixes the size, and `XXXNatUnknownSize*`, which pin the refusal's message; rows 400 and 446 have no test. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-unknown-size-arm/REPORT.md` section 10.

In the shorthand form, the checker refuses a clause that uses `x` as a `T`, and such a clause runs under walk only; a clause that does not, as in the library's `instanceOf`, passes. The binding form parses as the equality `x = e`. Only the specification's grammar has it, under the team's note that the section awaits the pattern-matching proposal (`typecase.tex:15`). 70	- F-73 **The compiled checker infers a generic's static arguments with coercion: a type parameter that is the whole type of each parameter it occurs in, as `T` in `pick[\T\](x: T, y: T)`, takes the narrowest type that every one of its arguments converts into and its bound permits.** It looks for that type among its arguments' types, their coercion targets and its bound, the bound only when it is a trait type other than `Object` or `Any`. It builds P-74 and P-49. A coerced declaration ranks below one that needs no coercion. A tie among coerced declarations is refused, "Ambiguous coercion", outside three narrow cases (the report's section 3.2). When the tied declarations differ only at positions where the call passes a numeral, the checker reads the numeral as `ZZ32`, or as `ZZ64` or `ZZ` when its value does not fit; that reading is a default. The coercion attempt refuses a call beyond 64 combinations of candidate types (row 506) and a call with an untyped function argument (row 507). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatLitArgChecker`, `CoercionGenericFnCompiledRungC` and `InferCoercionShapes`, which F-51 also cites, and the refusal of a tie by `XXXInferAmbiguousCoercion`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2.
71	- F-74 **Under walk, an integer numeral takes its type from its value: a `ZZ32` if it fits 32 bits, a `ZZ64` if it fits 64 bits, a `ZZ` above that; it stays so until walk has the checker's static types, since without them a list of numerals and a generic's static argument take their types from the values.** Its run-time type is the library's value object `Int`, `Long` or `BigNum`, below `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:125`, `:128`, `:223`). Walk instantiates a generic at it, so a `Box[\Int\]` is a type apart from `Box[\ZZ32\]` and dispatches past it (row 364). F-74 is why P-76's walk half waits; F-79 is the library half, built. Probe Q (`compile-ladder/plan-n/probe-q/PROBE-Q.md`) measured walk with every integer numeral an `IntLiteral`, the numeral's own type in the library. It ran before climb batch N's second run and before the library half landed. Alone, the switch changed 59 test verdicts. With four devices (a numeral at an `AnyIntegral` parameter read as `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, a tuple of numerals converted at dispatch, `asif` converting, a varargs list converted at dispatch), the library loaded and both microGPT checks kept their values, but 24 passing interpreter tests failed: 6 by design, 3 of them team tests that assert a `ZZ32`; 9 for want of static types (rows 364, 510); and 9 walk gaps. A size used as a value is a `ZZ32` up to 2^31-1 and a `ZZ64` above (row 486; F-140). Detail: `reviews/numeral-switch-judgement.md` sections 2 and 3.

P-49 decides the first and the third; the second and the fourth are an agent's choice, the instance-bound rung's (its decision record, D4). 80	- F-83 **In the interpreter's library, the string components `String.fss` and `FlatString.fss` hold no site of the distance, the compiled checker's errors in that library (F-53), and the rung's repairs of their refused declarations are in forms that the library already uses.** The trait `String` is declared in `FortressLibrary`, not in `String.fss`, which holds string objects and traits such as `CatString` and `SubString`. `String`'s api writes `abstract` on the members its component's trait leaves without a body or does not declare, and its `excludes` clause is the component's (F-286), so `String` has no entry in the `FortressLibrary` export error. `FlatString`'s api declares its component's header, `extends { String, DelegatedIndexed[\Char, ZZ32\] }`, and no `opr ||(a:FlatString, self)` (F-259). - F-117 **A compiled mutable variable's cell holds the language's top type, so a mutable variable of arrow type compiles and runs.** The cell holds `fortress.AnyType.Any`, not `FValue`, because a compiled closure is not an `FValue`. - F-121 **The team's spelling of `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause, `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]`, stays a comment, and no decision says whether it is a valid clause.** The live clause, which lists `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `NN32` and `NN64`, stands (P-44), and the compiled checker accepts it (F-62). - F-124 **On the compiled path, at or beyond the width of `ZZ32` or `ZZ64`, `LSHIFT` gives 0 and `RSHIFT` the sign; both reverse on a negative count, and `narrow` keeps the low 32 bits.** "The sign" is 0 for a nonnegative value and -1 for a negative one. `ZZ64`'s and `NN64`'s `narrow` to 32 bits keeps the low 32 bits. `<<`, `>>` and `<<<` keep their own rules, and `asZZ32` throws out of range. Negation, absolute value and division overflow only at the minimum value and test exactly for it, so the minimum raises `IntegerOverflow`, and `|0|`, `-0` and `0 DIV -1` answer 0. Addition and subtraction test the sign bits, and multiplication computes the exact product (`Math.multiplyExact` on `ZZ64`, a range-checked 64-bit product on `ZZ32`). So these raise `IntegerOverflow` on every overflow, and a zero factor answers 0. `ZZ`'s `<<<` raises a catchable `IntegerOverflow` on a shift that it cannot represent (row 386). Gated by `compiler_tests/IntSemanticsRungB.fss`, and for addition and subtraction by the team's `library_tests/Integer3.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-compiled/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-125 **Under `walk`, at or beyond the width of `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32` or `NN64`, `LSHIFT` gives 0 and `RSHIFT` the sign; both reverse on a negative count, and `ZZ`'s `shift` computes ⌊x·2^k⌋.** It builds P-69. "The sign" is 0 for a nonnegative value and -1 for a negative one. `ZZ`'s `shift(x, k)` is ⌊x·2^k⌋. A nonzero value shifted by a positive count beyond 2^31 - 1 raises a catchable `IntegerOverflow`, as does any result that the JVM's `BigInteger` cannot hold; zero shifted stays zero. The compiled path declares no `shift` (F-126). Gated by `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md` sections 4.3 and 4.4.

So the library's parameters that `shift` would shadow are named `amount`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/JUDGE.md` section 3; the renames, its `REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-128 **Under `walk`, the interpreter converts by coercion at its three kinds of type check.** They are a parameter, a varargs parameter included; an overloaded call that no declaration fits without coercion, which walk then dispatches again; and a typed binding or assignment. Not converted, as measured: a declared return (row 387), a coercion with its own static parameter (row 513), and an overloaded function's tuple parameter or a tuple-typed field (row 395). Not converted, by the code, and not measured: a varargs or keyword element of the specification's tuple coercion, and its arrow coercion. Gated by `tests/Coercion*RungC.fss`. Each size value, such as the 3 of `Vec[\3\]`, has one descriptor; in a run-time subtype test, it is a supertype only of an equal size. A size read as a value is a constant that the class loader replaces by the numeral. Closures and tasks capture a size as a free static parameter (F-135). A size made from a number known only at run time does not run compiled: `tests/NatReflectTest.fss` stops at load (row 307). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRt*`. Also open on the compiled path: a `ZZ32Vector` passed to a generic constructor fails at load (row 408); a dispatched overload arm whose static parameter has a concrete generic bound stops the compile in its sized form and dies at load in its type form (row 413); an object that extends two instantiations of one trait, one at a static parameter, passes the checker and dies at load (row 414). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 9.
- F-130 **The specification's wrapping operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰ are declared in the interpreter's library, and the library bodies and team tests that meant to wrap use them.** It builds P-73. The compiler prelude's ∔ and ∸ saturate, and it declares no ⨰ (row 348). One library body uses the operators where wrapping is wrong, by reading, not run (row 700). `Random`'s `LinearCongruential` computes `(mult DOTTIMES widen(state)) DOTPLUS add` and only then takes `MOD modulus`. So it agrees with the true state only where no step overflows or where the modulus divides 2^width of its type `N`. The library builds it only with the modulus 2^48, where it is right. Gated by `tests/WrapOperatorsRungD.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-wrap-operators/REPORT.md` section 2; their users, `reviews/wrap-dependent-code.md`.
- F-131 **The one library's number tower is flat.** It builds P-43. `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR64`, `RR32` and `IntLiteral` are siblings under `Number`. `IntLiteral` is the type that the library declares for an integer numeral. The compiled checker gives a numeral that type; walk still gives it `ZZ32`, or `ZZ64` or `ZZ` when its value does not fit (P-76). Each wider integer type converts from each narrower one, and `RR64` from a `ZZ32` and an `IntLiteral`; a `ZZ64` goes into `RR64` only when written out (P-74). `QQ` converts from the five integer types and `IntLiteral`, and `RR64` converts from `RR32` too (F-139). `NN32` does not yet convert into `RR64`: P-75 decides that it will. `Number`'s `=` compares a float with an exact number after `asFloat`, so it is not transitive (row 434). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/REPORT.md` sections 5 and 17.
- F-132 **Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit, as the specification says.** It builds P-73. Three kinds of operation raise nothing: the wrapping operators (F-130) and `narrow`, the written conversion of a `ZZ64` to `ZZ32` or an `NN64` to `NN32` (P-72), which keep the low bits; and the shifts `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT`, which lose the bits shifted out (F-125). The compiled path is outside this fact. Its known gaps: the compiler prelude's ranges raise `IntegerOverflow` where their bounds sum beyond `ZZ32` (row 453); and `^` saturates, throws an uncatchable Java exception or adds (rows 523 to 525). Its `CHOOSE` raises `IntegerOverflow` as walk's does (F-305). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-overflow-natives/REPORT.md` section 13; `compile-ladder/rung-size-range/REPORT.md` section 12.
- F-133 **The one library's scalar ranges are over `ZZ32` alone.** It builds P-77. In the interpreter's library, a range that reaches `ZZ32`'s minimum or maximum has the right size and elements, with no overflow, unless it is strided and a difference of its bounds leaves `ZZ32` (row 522, below). On the compiled path, the compiler library has no strided range (row 514), and its range `IN` and `=` are always `false` (rows 479, 481). When the compiled checker reads the one library, as every compiled program will after the switch-over, a `case` with no comparison operator compares by `=` where the specification gives ∈, so the clause never matches. This holds where the guard is typed by a type variable bounded by a `Contains` type (the library's trait of a membership `IN`, which ranges extend), or by a union of them (row 480); over the compiler library the checker picks ∈. Gated by `tests/RangeZZ32RungJ.fss`, `tests/RangeBoundsRungO.fss`, `tests/SeqRangeTopRungO.fss` and `tests/RangeEmptyHashRungO.fss`. Open under walk: a strided range whose elements fit, but a difference of whose bounds leaves `ZZ32`, raises `IntegerOverflow` at construction (row 522). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-ranges-zz32/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 10.
- F-134 **A typecase or catch clause's bound name is a local on the compiled path, so the compiled `cast[\T\]` matches a value of type `T`.** `cast[\ZZ32\](0)` still throws, because a numeral is not a `ZZ32`. Open: a name bound inside a clause's pattern (rows 340, 498), and a named clause or `catch` in a `do … also` arm that reads a captured variable (rows 497, 322). Gated by `compiler_tests/TypecaseBindRungG`, `CastBindRungG` and `library_tests/ClauseBindingRungB`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 10.
- F-135 **On the compiled path, a parallel task in a generic declaration is generic over its free static parameters.** These are the enclosing declaration's static parameters that the task uses. The code generator makes the task class generic over them, a template like a closure's class, which the class loader instantiates at the enclosing call's static arguments. So, in a generic method, the operands of an operator that the compiled path runs as parallel tasks, such as those of the concatenation `||`, run in such generic task classes. Walk makes no task classes. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRtTask` and `NatRtMethBoth`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-136 **On the compiled path, a generic top-level function, as an arm of a template dispatcher, is called at the dispatcher's own static parameters, by position, where it has as many static parameters as the dispatcher and each of the dispatcher's is a type.** Otherwise, by reading of `OverloadSet`, the dispatcher still reads the arm's static arguments from the argument's run-time value, as before the change. This is not measured for a count that differs, or for a dispatcher with a `nat`, `int`, `bool` or `opr` parameter (F-45). The arm's own kinds are not checked, so an arm with a `nat` parameter at a dispatcher's type parameter is not guarded out (by reading, not measured). Where one arm is more specific than another but does not line up with the dispatcher position by position, the dispatcher tests both at the call's static arguments, not at static arguments read from the value. So the less specific arm can run: through `viaT[\T\](x: T) = f(x)`, a `Box` runs `f[\T\](x: T)`, not `f[\U\](x: Box[\U\])`, and the checker accepts such arms where their return types agree (row 499, two expected failures). Generic dotted methods (row 495), and a generic declaration beside a plain one reached through an argument of static type `Any` (row 496), still die with `ClassCastException`. They die on an arm's static parameter left unrewritten, or on `ZZ32`, which the run time spells `…runtimeValues|FZZ32` and static code `fortress|CompilerBuiltin%ZZ32`. For template dispatchers both are fixed (rows 493 and 494). Gated by `compiler_tests/Dispatch*ArmRungG`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 7 and 9.
- F-137 **Under `walk`, a generic call's static arguments are inferred with coercion, by P-74's promotion, also for the declaration that an overloaded call chooses (P-46).** A lone type parameter is one that is the whole declared type of some argument and that no other argument fixes through a type such as `List[\T\]`. It takes the narrowest of its arguments' run-time types, their coercion targets and its bounds that admits every argument. Write it in the form of `explorations/reviews/batch-26-review.md` (read it first; its header says what it ran), as `explorations/reviews/batch-27-review.md`, owed by the coordinator skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing", step 3 (read that step):

Check the landed changes against the decisions on record (P-58, P-79, P-160, P-162 to P-168, with `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh`, and each entry's history where a claim rests on its reasons) and against the library's way, as the earlier reviews do; the specification's revisions too.

Climb batch 27 ended at 11:57 UTC (12:57 your time), and its push is held for your word.

**Should the hold on climb batch 27's push be lifted?**

- **Why it's held:** rung N's new `=` declarations stopped one team demo, `turnersParaffins0`. That's against your rule that every team demo keeps running. The workflow script holds the push on such a point, and only you can lift it.
- **The repair:** the judge ruled to fix walk and keep the demo as the team wrote it. Walk now calls an overloaded method on a value under `asif` (row 921), and all 52 demos reach their end again. The gate after the repair is green, with the distance at 0 and the checker count at 0.
- **One new thing:** the distance table shows two checker crashes in `FortressBuiltin`, at lines 661 to 773 and in the component's last stage. Climb batch 26's showed none. A crash can hide errors behind the zero. The post-batch review is finding which rung brought them, and whether they bear on the push.

The options:

1. **Lift it now.** I push the eight rungs and the repair, then run the record-landing workflow.
2. **Lift it once the review finds nothing against the push.** I push without asking you again. If the review finds something, I bring it to you first.

Option 1 lands about an hour sooner. Option 2 waits for the review's word on the crashes, and costs you nothing more.

I recommend 2.

What landed, one line each:

- `Number` is open: its `comprises` clause, `asFloat`, `=` and `exactValue` are gone. Each number type declares its own `asFloat` and an `=` for each conversion, 42 in all. The norm is declared at each of the eight types, and the specification is revised.
- The floats' natives over `Number` are declared at `RR64`, and six one-line helpers are added.
- The 16 integer shifts and powers convert in Fortress around bare bindings.
- `SEQV` follows the specification's rule on both paths. `Ratio`, `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` are value objects.
- Walk's loader answers `ilkName` and `SEQV`, and `asString` is `self.ilkName`. The ilk prints `ZZ32`, not `Int`. `match` takes any `String`.
- `Char`'s `asExprString` writes one text on both paths.
- The writer side runs over `JavaBufferedWriter`. `FileWriteStream` stays on glue until the reader rung.
- The code generator compiles `asif`: at a method call, at a call whose dispatched arguments are all assumptions, and as a value.
- Natives on glue went from 143 to 102.
- Rungs S and T never started, for want of disk. I've moved both to climb batch 28, which is on your review list.

input.prompt:
Load the `fortress-repo` skill first, with its parts `references/compiler.md`, `references/worktrees.md`, `references/build-and-caches.md` and `references/session.md`. This is a probe: you read, build and run in a worktree of your own, and edit no tracked file of `/home/user/fortress` (its `main` holds climb batch 27's unpushed landing; change nothing there, and do not build or run in it).

## The question

Climb batch 27's gate (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/gate/distance.txt`, on the merged tree at `151cb4126`, local `main` now at `209192b67`) reads `#total 0`, but no longer `#crash none` as climb batch 26's did (F-54). It holds two crash rows:

- `#crash decl ObjectDecl FortressBuiltin.fss:661:1-773:2 IllegalArgumentException Comparison method violates its general contract!` (the declaration is `value object Char`);
- `#crash stage component FortressBuiltin leftover InterpreterBug ** bug! Result of typechecking still contains intermediate nodes. Component at FortressBuiltin.fss:12.1`.

The post-batch review (`explorations/reviews/batch-27-review.md`, on the local `main`, its finding on the crashes) reads rung C (`wip/rung-char-expr-string`, `2f864ab0b`; worktree `/home/user/fortress-char-expr-string`), which ran neither the count nor the distance stage for want of disk, as the likely cause, by reading only.

Find, with evidence:

1. The crash's cause: the stack trace (the gate's logs: find where the gate stage wrote its distance log, under the main tree's `tmp/` or the gate's output folder named in `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js`; read, do not run, there), the comparator that breaks its contract, and which input of `Char`'s declaration feeds it, and which rung's change brought that input (C, or C with another rung's: E made `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` value objects and the code generator marks value objects; A changed walk's loader; F and I moved `Char`-adjacent bindings).
2. Whether it reproduces: run the distance stage (`explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh`, its header says how) on the merged tree, in a worktree of your own at `a2f0b5cf2` seeded from the base build (`explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh`, base build `/home/user/fortress-base27`) and built as `build-and-caches.md` says; and once on rung C's head if the cause is not plain from the first run. Say whether the crash is deterministic (a contract violation can depend on hash order: run the merged tree twice if the first run's cause is not plain).
3. Whether the crash hides errors: what of `Char`'s body and of the `FortressBuiltin` component's later stages the checker did not check because of it, and, if a one-line local change in your worktree avoids the crash, how many errors the distance then shows there (do not commit the change).
4. The ledger row to file (its text only; do not file it), and the facts made false (F-53, F-54, F-281, F-288 by the review).

Mind the disk: about 5.6G is free; remove your worktree when you are done (its branch, if you made one, need not be pushed or deleted). Write your report to `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/distance-crash/REPORT.md`. Your final message, at most 10 lines: the cause, the rung, deterministic or not, what it hides with the count of errors if you measured it, and whether a fix is small.

With either, `Char` is checked whole and the distance reads `#total 0`, `#crash none`: the crash hides 0 errors today.

F-53's figures stand, and its distance of 0 holds with `Char` checked whole.
  7. I could not write `REPORT.md`: the Write tool refused, saying a subagent returns its findings as text. The full report is below. I removed my worktree and made no branch; `main` is unchanged at `209192b67` and clean.
  
  ---
  
  # The distance's two crash rows on climb batch 27's merged tree: a probe
  
  I worked in `/home/user/fortress-distcrash`, a detached worktree at `a2f0b5cf2` seeded from `/home/user/fortress-base27` (`551b02858`). `ant compileAll` gave BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 35 s.   The evidence excerpts are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad/distance-crash/evidence/`. The scratchpad folder also holds `row.txt` and `rundist.sh`.
  
  ## 1. The cause
  
  **The gate's log.** The workflow sets `LOG_DIR='tmp/gate-batch-'+BATCH` (`climb-batch-workflow.js:1112-1113`), and the distance stage's scratch folder is `LOG_DIR/distance` (`:1860`). The crash is at `/home/user/fortress/tmp/gate-batch-27/distance/run.txt:762-768`. The log keeps only six frames, `TimSort.mergeLo(TimSort.java:781)` through `SeqOps.sorted(Seq.scala:728)`, because `tools/distance/shadow-patch.py:142` prints at most six.
  
  **The full stack.** I raised that limit to 400 in my worktree (run2; it changes only the printing):
  
  - `TimSort` → `sortWith` → **`Functionals.typedApplicationOfChecked(Functionals.scala:761)`** → `typedApplication(:660)` → `checkExprFunctionals(:1298)`, the operator case
  - → `Misc.handleIfClause(:127)` / `generatorClauseGetBindings(:73)`, an `if` condition → `Misc:528`, the `if`
  - → `Misc:435`, a block → `Decls.checkLetBody(:58)`, a local `x:ZZ32 = …` → `Misc:435` → `Misc:509`, a `do`
  - → `Decls.checkDecls(:221)`, a method body → `Decls.checkDecls(:165-168)`, the object's members in order
  - → `STypeChecker.typeCheck(:432)` → the shadow `StaticChecker` → `DistanceMulti.main(:68)`.

Over the 33 candidates the relation holds 231 pairs. It is irreflexive, never holds both ways, and is transitive, so it is a strict partial order. But incomparability is not transitive, in 3,880 triples. One of them:
  
  - `(BigNum, ZZ64) ≺ (BigNum, ZZ)`;
  - `(QQ, NN32)` is incomparable with both.
  
  TimSort checks only when it sorts 32 or more items; below that it sorts by insertion and checks nothing. Three other sorts use a partial order the same way: `Functionals.scala:728`, `CoercionOracle.scala:255`, and `Formula.scala:609`.   - 2 without coercion: `FortressLibrary.fsi:566`, ZZ32's `=` at `IntLiteral`, and `:69`, `=(Any, Any)`;
  - 31 with coercion.

  **The order.** The disambiguator builds the list of overloadings from a hash set: `toSet(env.unambiguousFunctionNames(op_name)) … .toList` (`ExprDisambiguator.scala:870-874`). An overloading's hash (`Overloading.java:117-130`) covers its unambiguous name, and a name's hash (`Id.java:80-89`) covers its text. That text holds the declaration's file, line and column, as `_|Library|FortressLibrary.fsi:700:5-31`.

  - **Not C.** In run inst2 I undid C's binding: `FortressBuiltin.fss:665` back to `Char$ToExprString`, which moves no line. The crash and the candidate order were identical. So I did not run C's head.

So `assertAfterTypeChecking` fires, which it does only when the component has no errors (`StaticChecker.java:264`). In runs inst4 and fix1, where `Char` is checked, neither row appears.

  | run | change | result | s |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | run1 | `run.sh` as tracked | both crash rows, `#total 0` | 137 |
  | run2 | 400 frames instead of 6 (printing only) | the same, with the full stack | 133 |

input.prompt:
Load the `fortress-repo` skill first (its committing part included). You change the batch workflow's script and manual, which are the coordinator's tools, not the original tree, so no Fortress test is owed; the script's own check is `explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` (its header says how to run it).

Work in a worktree of your own: `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add -b script/hold-after-repair /home/user/fortress-script-fix main`. Do not edit, commit or push in `/home/user/fortress` (another workflow lands there); commit on your branch by named paths with `fortress-repo`'s footer exactly (plain "Claude", no model name), and do not push. The coordinator lands your commit.

The files: `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js` and its manual `explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`. Read the manual's sections that bear (with `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md#<heading>'`) and the coordinator skill's `.claude/skills/coordinator/references/batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs", whose rules the script must follow.

## 1. A point that the repair fixed holds no push (the curator's word, 2026-11-07)

In climb batch 27 (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/RECORD.md`, its paragraph "Not pushed"; `JUDGE-review.md`; `REPAIR-review.md`; the run's journal `/root/.claude/projects/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/subagents/workflows/wf_72601264-7dd/journal.jsonl`), the merged-diff review returned a point with `holdsPush: true`: a team demo stopped on the merged tree, against P-79. Its judge ruled a repair, the repair fixed walk, all 52 demos reached their end again, and the gate after the repair was green. Yet `pushHeldBy` (`climb-batch-workflow.js`, about line 2084) still held the push, since it reads the review's `pointsReached` with no regard to the repair. The curator: "When it was fixed, then it should land."

Change the script so that a `holdsPush` point that a repair round settled no longer holds the push. The push stays held only by a point that cannot be undone, by a point that still acts against a decision on record after the repairs, or by a gate that stays red after its repair (`batch.md`, "Reserved points and repairs"). Design it so that the script, not an agent's prose, decides: for example, the repair role's schema returns, for each `holdsPush` point it was given, whether its repair settled it, with the evidence, and `pushHeldBy` drops the settled ones; a point marked as one that cannot be undone is never dropped. Keep the change small and in the script's style. Update the manual's text on the hold to match.

## 2. The footer

Commit `b9635f0a7` (the judge's ruling on the merged-diff review) carries a model name in its `Co-Authored-By` line, against `fortress-repo`'s `references/committing.md`; the agent followed the harness's attribution reminder. The commit stage's footer check (about line 2139) saw it and let it pass. Make every role that commits carry, in its prompt, the exact footer and the line that it overrides any footer that the harness suggests; and make the commit stage's check name such a commit as a defect in its result (it must not rewrite pushed or cited history; a report line that the coordinator routes is enough).

## 3. The disk

The disk allowance ran out during climb batch 27, so rungs S and T never started and other stages skipped their measures (the RECORD's "Not landed" and PLAN's item 68). Add a check at the run's start, before the scatter: read the free space on `/home/user` (`df -P`), and if it is under a floor of about 1.5G per rung plus 4G, stop the run with a clear message before any agent starts, so the coordinator frees disk and launches again. Put the floor's numbers in one constant with a comment of its ground, and state the check in the manual.

Run `workflow-scenarios.js` until it reports 0 problems, and parse the script as its header says. Your final message, at most 10 lines: the commit on your branch, what each of the three changes does, and the scenarios check's result.

content.content:
## Landing its result

The workflow lands its own result, by the curator's rule of 2026-11-03 (`../../HELD.md`, "Held in chat (2026-11-03)", 06:2x); the design's decision 6, the coordinator's cherry-pick, is reversed. After the judge, the lander, in the main tree:

1. Checks the judge's checks: the branch holds its commits past AT, `mech-final.md` says "Every check passes.", the worktree is clean. If one fails, it lands nothing, and the result's `stopped` says so; the worktree and the branch stay.
2. Puts the commits on `main`: `git merge --ff-only` of the branch when `main` is still at AT, which keeps the judge's hashes; otherwise `git cherry-pick AT..BRANCH`, since `main` moved during the run. A refusal or a conflict is aborted, `main` stays where it was, and the run stops as in step 1.
3. Runs on `main` `record.py check --base <main before the landing>`, `ledger.py landing-check <the batch's base>` and `check-index.sh`. If one fails, `git reset --keep` takes the run's commits off the local `main`, which is not pushed, and the run stops as in step 1.
4. Pushes, in the order of the `fortress-repo` skill's committing part: `git log origin/main..main` lists only the run's commits, then `main`, `main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8` and `main:blinded-fable`. A refused push, or another agent's commit in that list, stops the run, landed but not all pushed, before the orientation update.
5. `git worktree remove` the worktree, without `--force`, and `git branch -D` the branch.
6. Reads the facts list of the orientation call in the landed `diff.md`'s "Next" (the entries that the landing and the run added or changed); the script then runs `orientation.js` with `mode: 'update'`, `out` the batch's `climb-batch-N/orientation/` and `stream` `orientation-bN`. Nothing waits on the coordinator between the record's commits and the update. With no entry there, the update is skipped, and the skill update still runs. If the update fails to start, the run stops, landed and pushed, before the skill update. The skill update below installs its result.

content.content:
## Preparing a batch record

An Opus planning worker drafts `CLIMB-BATCH-<n>.md`. A Fable reviewer edits it in place with one reason per change. The coordinator reads the diff and brings the record's questions to the curator one per message. The batch launches on the answers or on the standing go (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The go").

The planner builds each rung's briefing as in-context learning: the agents were not trained on Fortress, and the language was never finished (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). A briefing holds what the rung's section cites: the decisions and earlier rulings it rests on, its ledger rows, the specification's sections whole by their headings, the notes on the subject by section, and the library code that is the precedent. Process positions and harness facts stay out, because the brief's role text and the skill carry them. In batch 10 the workers named none of the 87 POSITIONS and FACTS keys before their fix edits (`process-engineering/context-study.md`, section 5). Each key goes through `facts-extract.sh --check` on the base, every key matching exactly one place. Each carries one line on why it is there. The planner marks the `checks` sub-list: the decisions and rows the checks need, and the sections and precedent code they compare against.

A rung that changes what an implementation does is briefed with the Appendix I Effects and the specification's notes that its change makes false, found by a grep while the record is prepared. Batch 9's record gave rung K none, and Appendix I's `comprises` Effect was that batch's one blocking finding (`reviews/batch-9-review.md`, finding 3).

A record asks a rung for no corpus-wide output comparison, no ladder before-run, no microGPT check and no specification build log (P-103, "The suite's verdict is the check."; the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "What a brief holds"). Whole suites are the skill's rule (`tests-running.md`, "When to run a whole suite"). A count of the programs a change reaches, when a decision needs one, is the planner's probe, taken before the record is written. A named one-time count of changed outputs is asked only where a decision of the curator's names it for that rung. The coordinator starts its base pass before the launch (`tools/count-run/count-run.sh`).

A ledger note that the record briefs fits its row: the planner reads the row with `ledger.py show N` against the tool's limits (notes 700 characters, the row 1,200) and, where the note does not fit, briefs the row's whole new line. Climb batch 26's record briefed rung S a note to row 440, whose notes held 676 of 700 characters (`reviews/batch-26-review.md`, process finding 6).

The record's section on how it is run gives the manifest's fields rung by rung, the intro every agent reads, and the launch steps. It holds no copy of the block: the batch's generator writes the block from the record.

## Before the launch

The coordinator, in this order:

1. The script, this manual and the batch's manifest generator on `main`. The base is `main`'s head after them, by its full hash, passed as `args.base`.
2. The batch's one base build, a worktree at the base outside the main tree, built once and then left alone. Every rung worktree is seeded from it, and the old code runs from it (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The workflow"). About 200 s, as the skill's `worktrees.md`, "Finding or building a base build", gives it:

        git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add --detach /home/user/fortress-base<N> <base>
        cd /home/user/fortress-base<N>      # then set up the call as the skill's build-and-caches.md says
        ant compileAll                      # BUILD SUCCESSFUL
        # the library order (build-and-caches.md, "The library order"), then one walk run, which warms walk's caches:
        bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
        git status --porcelain              # empty: the seed refuses a base build that is not clean

   Its path goes to the launch as `args.baseBuild`. The script refuses to start without it (scenario B1).
3. One trial seed proves the base build, about 3 s: `explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck - <base>`, then `git -C /home/user/fortress worktree remove /home/user/fortress-seedcheck`. One `old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base<N> /home/user/fortress-seedcheck-caches ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss`, run from the main tree, proves the old code runs; its folder is removed after.
4. The briefings checked on the base (`python3 explorations/compile-ladder/plan-<N>/manifest/lists<N>.py`). The block generated (`gen<N>.py`), checked in a scratch copy and spliced (`check<N>.js`, then `check<N>.js --write`). Then `node explorations/coordinator/tools/workflow-scenarios.js` on the spliced script, which also checks that every skill section the script cites by name is a heading of the skill. Then the commit.
5. `df -P /home/user`, its Available column at or above the script's floor, 1.5 G a rung plus 4 G ("The disk before the scatter"), which the script reads again before the scatter and stops under. `git status --porcelain` empty in the main tree, and no other agent writing there or pushing `main` while the run gathers and commits. The session's permission rules let the commit stage run `tools/mg-run.sh`.
6. Check-ins armed for the run's length, 45 minutes apart (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`, "Watching a run").

The launch: `Workflow({scriptPath: 'explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js', args: {base: '<full hash>', baseBuild: '/home/user/fortress-base<N>'}})`. The args are kept byte for byte, since a resume needs them. The base build stays until the coordinator removes it after the landing.

The record-landing for climb batch 27 is finished, and the revival page is republished at version 29: https://claude.ai/artifact/8Gg1f2ZRXg462qmhcwx1T5

POSITIONS changed in eight entries, one line each:

- **P-160:** the removal of `Number`'s clause and `asFloat` is now stated as done, citing F-324.
- **P-163:** the binding's and the parser's line numbers are updated. The sentence on what would change when the rung landed is dropped.
- **P-165:** the vector norm is now stated as declared at each of the eight number types, by its own `asFloat`. That's the fork's default, on your review list. The specification's revised lines are cited.
- **P-166:** `Ratio` is now stated as a value object. The clause on which rung would do it is dropped.
- **P-167:** "once the compiled path reads the one library" is added before the stack-overflow clause. "The rung works out the way" is dropped, and it now points to P-169.
- **P-168:** rows 906 and 907 are fixed, and the prelude's own `===` keeps row 908 until the switch-over. The `CC64` test now exists (F-326).
- **P-58:** it now states that walk's loader answers P-167's 2 names and P-169's 45 with walk's own operations.
- **P-169, new:** your Q1 decision through the Fable judgement. The runtime's own 45 natives name compiled helpers that walk's loader answers with walk's own operations, in three compiled shapes. The array store's shape stays your open question, Q2. Its detailed review is queue item 406.

The words are in these commits:

- https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/commit/d131d92c5
- https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/commit/51c30d263

Climb batch 28's planner started at about 16:45 UTC (17:45 your time). It runs the probes for the remaining natives, including a measurement of Q2's two store shapes. Before the launch, I'll bring you Q2 and Q3, one per message, each with its measurement.

import re

s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('**State at 14:0x UTC on 2026-11-07**')

His Q1 decision is P-169 (`51c30d263`, queue item 406 for his detailed review; Q2 is item 407; PLAN's D2, N3, N5 and `getProgramArgsPrim` lines routed at `5d5c95dfe`). The batch script holds no push that its repair settled and reads the disk before the scatter (`3ef9a5fc9`). The footer rule is in `fortress-repo`'s committing part (`da13260ed`, `b1cdb209d`): a commit already made whose footer names a model is left as it is, never checked, reported or listed. The coordinator runs on Opus since about 06:45; it read FACTS and POSITIONS whole at 12:0x and the record-landing's POSITIONS changes after it (reported to him at 16:5x).

- **The planner of climb batch 28** (an Opus Agent-tool worker at extra-high effort, launched about 16:45): `explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-28.md` and its probes under `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-28/`, committed on `main`, not pushed. Later: Q4 (`Reflect`'s 28, default stay walk-only); PLAN's items 69 to 72; item 68 (the coordinator's defaults: the disk freed, S and T moved to climb batch 28); the strings question; the ledger pass review's decisions once written.

## Next, in order

2. The page worker's report: one line to him with the commits and the page's link.
3. The ledger pass review he asked for at 10:1x on 11-06 (`explorations/reviews/ledger-pass-review-2026-11-06.md`, never landed), when the work leaves room; then the follow-ups file's 37 items.
4. '''

- **Traits and objects.**
  - The old text did not say what `=` does when a type declares none. It now says that `=` is then `SEQV`: a value object compares field by field, and a string only to itself.
  - It also says where to write the `I extends Index` bound until the switch-over.
- **Numbers.**
  - The old text gave an example that walk now prints differently. It now says that walk prints `Cell[\ZZ32\]` for a value that is a `Cell[\Int\]`.
  - New rule: `Number` declares nothing. Generic code over `T extends Number` can call nothing on a `T`.
  - New rule: two numbers of different types are `=` only through a coercion. Otherwise the answer is `false`.

The new `sources.md` section, "Climb batch 27's update", holds the provenance.

content.content:
# A lost container

This part is for the coordinating session. Record no gap-ledger row for a lost container: it is not a gap of the tree.

The platform can reclaim, corrupt or rebuild a container at any time. What was pushed survives, the backup's transcripts included. Everything else on its disk is lost: worktrees, uncommitted edits, unpushed commits, logs, and every running agent. A run of agents whose script and briefs are committed can run again.

## Re-provisioning

The platform rebuilds a container from the branch that the session was created from, `blinded-fable` for the coordinating session. `get_session` shows it, as `session_context.sources[].git_repository.revision`. If the branch is behind `main`, the new container starts on a stale tree. If the branch is gone, the clone fails: the platform shows "The requested branch or commit was not found in the repository", and the repository holds only an empty `.git`.

- To check the branch, run `git fetch origin && git rev-parse origin/main origin/blinded-fable`. If the two hashes differ, push as `fortress-repo`'s `references/committing.md` says, which pushes `main` to it.

A rebuilt container comes up blank: no other folder under `/home/user`, JDK 21 alone, no `ant`, no backup worktree and no `~/.claude/settings.json`. To restore it:

1. Run `git fetch origin main`, then `git checkout -b main origin/main`.
2. Run `explorations/experiment/setup.sh`. In about 4 minutes, it installs JDK 25 and `ant`, builds the tree and re-arms the backup.

If the session cannot go on, start a new session in a container that has the checkout and the toolchain. Fast-forward that checkout to `main`, re-arm the backup (below), and go on from what was pushed and from the old session's transcript (below).

- Only one container at a time may back up to a branch. While one does, the pushes of a second to the same branch are refused.
- A session resumed in a rebuilt container can start from a shortened copy of its transcript. The new container's first snapshot then commits that copy over the full transcript. The full one stays in the branch's history: copy it from the commit before that snapshot to `<session>.until-<UTC time>.jsonl.parts/` on the branch, and let the later transcript go on at the usual path.

## Re-arming the backup

    git -C /home/user/fortress fetch origin transcripts-blinded:transcripts-blinded
    git -C /home/user/fortress worktree add /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded transcripts-blinded
    /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/scripts/backup.sh --run     # one pass, in the foreground
    tail -1 /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/.backup.log         # verify

The tracked `.claude/settings.json` already registers the hook (`hooks.md`). The pass is good when the log's line reads `copier_rc=0` and either `commit=<hash>` with `push=ok`, or `commit=none ahead=0 push=none`. `--run` waits for a runner at work, then makes its pass.

Sessions created from `blinded-fable` back up to `transcripts-blinded`. Earlier coordinating sessions are on `transcripts`. If you arm a backup to `transcripts`, first copy the reference copies (`hooks.md`) into its `scripts/`. Never merge the two branches. When you search the transcripts, search both.

## Reading another session's transcript

Any session reads another's from the backup branches, with no switch or clone. `<b>` is `transcripts` or `transcripts-blinded`:

    git fetch origin transcripts transcripts-blinded
    git show origin/<b>:projects/-home-user-fortress/<session>.jsonl | head
    git grep -l 'some string' origin/transcripts origin/transcripts-blinded -- 'projects/*'

- A transcript up to 64 MiB is `<session>.jsonl`. A larger one is stored as `<session>.jsonl.parts/NNN.jsonl`, cut at line ends. Join it with `cat <session>.jsonl.parts/*.jsonl`.
- Workflow agents' transcripts and journals are under `projects/<project>/<session>/subagents/workflows/<run>/`, and the launched scripts under `projects/<project>/<session>/workflows/scripts/`.
- For a long search, check a branch out as a worktree, a second copy on disk, after you check Avail (`machine.md`): `git worktree add /home/user/fortress-transcripts transcripts`.

## Recovering the work

1. For each branch that the lost container worked on, find its last pushed commit: `git fetch origin && git log -1 --format='%h %ci' origin/<branch>`. Nothing after it is safe.
2. On the backup branch, read the tail of the lost session's transcript, its last part. Work after its last record cannot be recovered.
3. In that tail, find the edits after the last push, the `Edit`, `Write` and `Bash` calls that change files, and replay them by hand.
4. Recover Workflow scripts and briefs from the transcript: a `Workflow` `tool_use` record holds its whole script.
5. Do not try to resume a Workflow run: only the session that launched it can (the `coordinator` skill's `references/delegating.md`).
6. Before you continue, write down where the work stands, from the transcript's tail and not from memory.
