<!-- What is established about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as it stands now, grouped by area: each entry the fact, its source and its test. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `FACTS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before. What an entry holds and how it is written: the `coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`. -->

# Facts on record

## Execution model

- F-7 **Walk and the compiled path share the parser and the phases, and only the compiled path runs the static type checker.** Walk switches the checker off, and no switch turns it on. So walk checks no static types of expressions: an ill-typed expression shows only when it runs, as a failed dispatch or as another run-time error, such as F-239's refusal of an `if` on a value that is not a `Boolean`. At load, walk refuses some ill-formed declarations: the `fortress-repo` skill's `interpreter.md`, "What walk checks", lists them, with their evidence in F-29 (`comprises` clauses), F-142 (the Meet Rule for Functional Methods) and F-145 (uncovered abstract methods and `override`). The phases and where the two paths part: the skill's "How a program runs". Detail: `explorations/repo-internals.md`, "The two worlds".
- F-9 **`fortress typecheck` checks a program against the compiler's library, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, so it is no oracle for walk programs.** `Shell.java` calls `useCompilerLibraries()` for the command (row 69). P-12 has walk run the checker on its own programs after the switch-over, and walk cannot do so as it stands: it runs with type checking and the Scala checker off, the Java checker is gone (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:228-229`), and it has no case for the `CoercionInvocation` nodes that the checker inserts, by reading (row 833).
- F-11 **The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main representational cost of microGPT-shaped array code.** So a compiled `RR64` loop holds no `dadd` or `dmul` (the `fortress-repo` skill, "The compiled runtime"). In Java models of microGPT's three kernels, boxed elements cost 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`. No such kernel compiles yet: the compiler prelude has no array type (row 305), and the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (P-37). In a hot compiled loop, escape analysis removes the temporary boxes, and one box per assignment to a mutable variable per iteration stays (F-301), as long as C2's inline depth reaches each box's constructor chain (F-302). Detail: `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 4; `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` section 4.
- F-12 **On the compiled path, the scalar `RR64` loop `bench1t` ran in 0.74 s in one session's measurement; the loop still pays for its generator, for boxing and for a transaction check at each use of its accumulator.** `bench1t` is `for i <- seq(1#20000000) do acc := acc 0.9999999 + 0.0000001 end` on a `var acc: RR64`, with both literals written in the loop. The time is the median of three loop-only runs at one thread (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`, "The four timings"). Times taken in different sessions differ on this machine, so compare only times from one session. What the loop does, read in its bytecode (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` sections 4 and 5): the `seq` loop becomes the compiler prelude's `countedseqloop`, which runs the iterations in order by a recursive split over boxed indices, with a closure call per element; each value is boxed (F-11); and the accumulator is a volatile cell whose read and write each first call `BaseTask.inATransaction`, as for every mutable local (F-40, what a size costs at run time, whose sized loop pays the same check). Within the boxing and the cell, the report counts four allocations per iteration, an interface call to the native wrapper and the casts, the part that unboxed doubles and `double[]` would attack. No share of the 0.74 s is measured.
- F-17 **The bytecode cache can come up empty after a library order that reports exit 0.** Running the same commands again, one at a time, made the jars. The cause is not known. Check the five jars before a compiled run (the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md`, "The library order"). Detail: `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-18 **On the compiled path, the class loader makes the class of a generic instantiation at its first use, by rewriting the template's bytecode with ASM, and the rewriting only renames, so it gives no instance a `double[]` field.** The class is `InstantiatingClassloader`; the `fortress-repo` skill's "The compiled runtime" gives the mechanism. A size is part of the made class's name, as in `pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, the object `Box` at size 3 in the probe component `pNatMeth`. Inside the class, the size's descriptor is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` (F-129). A field of the template's type `T`, `LT;`, becomes `LFRR64;` in `Box⟦FRR64⟧`, and `[D` is no class name, so stamping alone keeps every number boxed (F-11). The team's direction for unboxing builds on this class per instantiation (the plan in `compiler/optimization/Unbox.java`; the loader's empty "expando" stub, `runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java:168-172`), but a loader that stamps an `RR64` instance with a `double[]` field, way A4 of array decision A (P-85), does not exist and is unmeasured. Walk instantiates generics in its own evaluator, not by classes. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` section 1; `coordinator/array-design.md` section 2 (probe 1); `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 3, way A4.
- F-19 **By the specification, the iterations of a `for` loop, the elements of a tuple, and the arguments of a call or an operator may run in parallel, and a program must assume that they do.** A `for` loop is sequential only if every generator is, as `seq(g)` or `sequential(g)` makes it. An implementation may also run them one after another (`evaluation/parallelism.tex:88-90`), so a program cannot count on parallel runs either. For the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator, each path starts a task only where it judges it worth it: walk by `TupleTask.worthSpawning`, which also governs a call's arguments, and the code generator by `ParallelismAnalyzer`. Compiled, a function call's arguments run in order (`CodeGen.evalArg`). A `for` loop over a range without `seq` runs by splitting the range into `do … also do … end` blocks. Under walk, every such block is a task, and walk's library splits down to single elements (`Library/RangeInternals.fss`). Compiled, the first block runs in place, and each other block forks only where `BaseTask.forkIfProfitable` judges it worth it, as tuple elements do; the compiler prelude's `parloop` splits down to `FORTRESS_LOOP_CHUNK` elements, 1 by default. `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the pool of worker threads (the `fortress-repo` skill, "Parallelism and mutable state"). By grep, no program under `explorations/`, the model programs and the probes, writes `spawn`, which starts an explicit thread, or an `also do` block, so their parallelism comes only from loops, tuples and arguments. The revival's tests under `ProjectFortress/` write both. Source: `Specification/basic/expressions/for.tex:28-32`, `tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:58-59`, `evaluation/parallelism.tex:50-80`.
- F-20 **Sizes, the `nat` and `int` static parameters, are values at run time; they check shapes, and no optimization uses them (F-40, what a size costs at run time).** The compiled checker checks them (F-67), and a sized program loads and runs compiled (F-129). Under walk, `Vector` and `Matrix` take their sizes from an array built at run time: `f[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\])` takes `s` from `array[\RR64\](3)`, and overloads on `Vector` and `Matrix` dispatch by rank (row 214). The array-type syntax `T[n]` with a `nat` parameter does not unify with such an array, "Cannot unify … with ArrayType", where `T[3]` with a literal size does (row 23). Walk matches sizes at dispatch. A mismatch, such as a `DOT`, the library's inner product, of a 2×3 matrix by a 2×3 matrix, whose inner sizes differ, is a `ProgramError`, "Failed to find any matching overload", that no `catch` takes (row 254). Source: `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:96`.
- F-21 **The February 2011 Working Draft's bare `Nothing`, one object for every `T`, is accepted on neither path: the grammar refuses its `excludes` clause, and without that clause `T` is undefined.** The declaration is `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/convenience.tex:40`). Both paths stop at a syntax error at `excludes`, since an object has no `excludes` clause (measured: `reviews/spec-refused-examples.md`, E4). Without that clause, both report `T is undefined` at the `T` of the `extends` clause: a `where` clause on an object binds no type variable of its `extends` clause, as row 17 holds for a trait. Today's specification refuses the form in any case, by instantiation exclusion, and marks it "Not allowed" beside the parametric `Nothing[\T\]` that the interpreter's library writes (F-167). P-90 still calls the bare `Nothing` future work that waits for such `where` clauses, not tried before then. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-maybe/REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-22 **When a component's name differs from the api that it exports, neither path finds the component, for an exported function or variable alike.** The specification resolves an imported api to any component that exports it (`Specification/basic/components/overview.tex`). The tree looks only under the api's name, unless a user maps the api to its component by hand with `LinkShell`'s `alink` or `clink`. The linker's component repository looks this way (`Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`), so `fortress link` and walk print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path" before any code is generated. The code generator names a reference to an exported declaration after the api, and the declaring class after the component. The link step rewrites such a reference to the component only when the repository names it, so files compiled one by one, without `fortress link`, die with `NoClassDefFoundError`. The missing step is the repository's: finding the component that exports the api. The report names two repairs, neither built: the repository could search the source path for that component, or the code generator could emit api-named forwarders, for which three comments in `CodeGen.java` leave a place. Walk and `fortress link` need the first. Workaround: name the api after its component. Gated by the expected failure `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test` (row 320). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-export-var/REPORT.md`, "The measurement that separates them".
- F-23 **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it.** The parser's `createSpan` trims back over spaces only, and a declaration that ends in `end` is unaffected (row 359). So a comment-only library edit can change the syntax tree, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics maps positions back first. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md` section 6, D1.
- F-24 **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees.** It throws a `FortressError` that holds the exception's object, as `Int.overflow()` does for `IntegerOverflow` (F-132; row 347, fixed). A native bound to a helper of `nativeHelpers/` raises the library's own exception where the helper raises a class of the compiled prelude, such as `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$DivisionByZero`, so `DIV`, `REM` and `MOD` by zero on `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `NN32` and `NN64` raise `DivisionByZero` (F-299, F-306, F-308, F-312). Any other Java exception of a native becomes a `ProgramError`, which no `catch` takes. Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`, and for a helper by `tests/NativeHelperRaiseWalk.fss` and, for each of the five types, `tests/<type>DivisionByZeroWalk.fss` and `tests/<type>RemainderByZeroWalk.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md` section 4.1.
- F-25 **On the compiled path, the class loader loads each class under the JDK's class-loading lock, so the first load of an instantiation's class is safe on four threads at once.** `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` holds `getClassLoadingLock(name)` for the whole load, as the JDK's own `ClassLoader.loadClass` does. Without the lock, two threads that first loaded such classes at the same time could race, and the run died with a `NullPointerException` (row 417, fixed). The test `compiler_tests/FirstLoadThreadsRungG` calls the generic overload `f[\T\](v: Vt[\T\])` at eight instantiations, `Vt[\A1\]` to `Vt[\A8\]`, from a parallel `for` loop of 800 iterations. Observed: at four threads it failed 5 runs of 5 before the lock, and passed 5 of 5 after. It is one of the gate's atomic runs, which run each program at four threads (`gate.md`). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 (the runs) and 12 (why this lock).
- F-26 **Under walk, when one of two applicable declarations has static parameters of its own, the call chooses on their declared domains where exactly one lies inside the other, not by the order in which they are written.** It builds P-45, the choice among overloads by declared parameter types, under walk. A declaration has static parameters of its own if it is a generic function or constructor, or a functional method with static parameters in a trait or object without any. Its declared domain, walk's symbolic instance, is its parameter types with each type parameter standing for itself under its bounds. Where neither declared domain lies inside the other, where each lies inside the other, or where neither declaration has static parameters of its own, walk compares the domains of the instances that the call makes. So a functional method of a generic trait or object is compared on its instance, and a generic dotted method is chosen by F-253 (a generic method at a dotted call, also chosen on declared domains). If the chosen declaration is generic and its instance takes an argument only by a conversion, walk converts the argument and dispatches the converted arguments again, so the most specific declaration for the converted values runs. In two cases walk keeps the chosen instance, with no second dispatch: an overloaded dotted method, and a position whose conversion `Coercions.coercionFor` does not find, such as a tuple converted element by element. Two generic overloads whose static parameters agree in name, kind and bounds share one symbolic instance, even if their `where` clauses differ; no test or library declaration has such a pair (row 478). Gated by `tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss` and `DispatchConvertedAgain.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.1, 5.2 (the second dispatch) and 5.5 (the symbolic instance).
- F-27 **Walk's load check reads again two kinds of overload pair that its parameter-by-parameter check refuses, and accepts those that pass: a generic declaration beside a plain one, read on their declared domains, and two plain top-level functions, not methods, whose overlap other declarations cover through `comprises` clauses.** To test a cover, the check cuts the overlap of the two domains, position by position, into parts by the `comprises` clauses. Each combination of parts must lie inside the domain of one declaration without static parameters that lies below both. So several such declarations may together cover the overlap. A search that does not settle refuses. A generic declaration beside a plain one passes where one declared domain lies strictly inside the other and the inner one's return type lies below the outer one's. Where neither lies inside the other, the pair needs the same cover, or declared domains that exclude each other read whole (F-258, exclusion over the whole parameter type). Equal declared domains are refused. It builds under walk P-46, by which a conversion never changes which declaration runs when one already fits, and P-60, by which several declarations below both may cover a meet. Two generic declarations are read on their declared domains too (F-252: the No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet Rules, each over its own instances). Walk still refuses the valid example of the POPL 2019 paper on symmetric multiple dispatch (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`, p. 11:13), a set of three generic declarations (row 539). Gated by `tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss` and `GenericBesidePlain*.fss`, among others. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.3 (generic beside plain) and 5.4 (the cover).
- F-28 **Walk instantiates a generic declaration declared to return `Any`.** `MakeInferenceSpecific` treats `Any` as it treats a trait type (row 157, fixed). Its visitor has no case for 11 of the syntax tree's 18 concrete type classes, and of those only the dimension forms can be written as a return type. Gated by `tests/GenericReturningAny.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 3.
- F-29 **Under walk, the load check refuses a trait or object that extends a closed trait of the program's main component where the trait's `comprises` clause does not allow it.** A closed trait is one with a `comprises` clause. The check reads every trait and object of every component of the program, the library's included, as a possible extender. An extender is allowed in three cases: it lies below a listed type; it is a trait whose own `comprises` clause lists only types that are allowed in turn; or it is a generic trait that some trait or object extends, and each of those extenders lies below a listed type (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations"). The check does not yet read a clause declared outside the main component, the library's among them (row 551), or an object expression's `extends` clause (row 597). Nor does it check that each listed type extends the trait at every instantiation (row 598). A check that read the library's clauses would refuse at load every program that imports the library's `Reflect` (row 595), and three team tests and two demos whose objects extend `Exception` directly (row 596). Their repairs come before that check and are the curator's. Gated by `tests/ComprisesUnlistedExtender` and `ComprisesGenericChildUnlistedExtender`, refused at load, and by the `XXX` tests of rows 487 (a type of another component below a generic subtrait of a closed trait), 551, 597 and 598, which stay green while walk still loads their programs. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-load-check/REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-269 **Under walk, a program's declarations of a library operator name are checked against the library's only when the program declares two or more of that name, and only on a cold cache.** One such declaration is not checked. Two or more are checked with the library's declarations, and the check can refuse them beside the library's generic declarations, even where they are more specific than the library's. It refused C4's former pair of `MAX` between an `RR64` and an `Array[\RR64,I\]`, in both orders, which C4 dropped when F-119's scalar extension took its place (row 341). It refuses the `Matrix`-specialised elementwise `×` of `apl/mg/elemwise_nat_probe.fss` (F-155). Walk writes a component to its cache before it runs this check, and skips the check on a component that it reads back. So a refusal appears once, on a cold cache, and never again (row 342). The check runs only when walk analyses the library itself again: deleting the program's own cache entries does not bring it back (row 342). So a test that depends on this check must run from an empty cache. Detail: rows 341 and 342; `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md` section 4, a gated run that met a warm cache.
- F-291 **With the bound `Any`, the compiled path compiles, loads and runs generics at tuple and arrow static arguments as it does with `extends Any` written; `()` fails whatever the bound (row 339), and so does a generic dotted method with one tuple-typed parameter (row 832).** Measured once: generic functions, objects and traits, dispatch to a generic arm and `typecase`, at a pair or an arrow, with the static argument written or inferred. The class loader made the same classes by name, and the program jars read the same under `javap`, as the same programs with `extends Any` written under the compile command's bound `Object`. So the switch to the bound `Any` costs the run time no work for these shapes; its test cost is F-292. Not run: the one library's own instantiations at tuples, tuples of three or more and nested ones, generic functional methods at a tuple, a native that receives a tuple. With `extends Object` written, they are refused, or pass unchecked where the static argument is written (row 470); the compile command's bound is `Any` (`Shell.java:372`). No gated test. Detail: `perf-probes/bound-any-compiled/REPORT.md`, "The shapes by setting" and "What the class loader makes".
- F-301 **On the compiled path a native helper is called through a generated wrapper over the box classes, and once the loop is hot C2 inlines the whole path, so the call costs nothing of its own.** A binding `builtinPrimitive("pkg.Class.method")` and a written `import java` alias call compile to the same bytes: an `invokestatic` of `native.pkg.Class.method`, a class the compiled path writes into `nativewrapper_cache/`, which unboxes each argument with `getValue`, calls the helper and boxes its result with `make`, a new box each time (`compiler/nativeInterface/FortressMethodAdapter.java:303-327`; `compiler/runtimeValues/FZZ32.java:22-24`). A functional method such as `ZZ32`'s `+` reaches the wrapper through the dispatcher, an interface call, the springboard and the trait's static body. C2 inlines all of these frames, the helper, `make` and the box's constructor chain; only C1's profiling code refuses the helper and the chain's deep frames. Escape analysis then removes every temporary box, a helper's result passed into another helper among them, and one box stays per assignment to a mutable variable per iteration: 16 bytes for a `ZZ32`, 24 for an `RR64`. The library's form and the prelude's allocate the same. Observed once on one small program, `perf-probes/helper-calls/HelperCalls.fss`, by `javap`, C2's inlining log and the bytes that JFR counted, with no timing, on a machine shared at a load of 20 to 25; no test checks it. Detail: `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` sections 2 to 5.
- F-302 **In those loops C2 inlines down to depth 12 from the loop, against the 16 at which it stops by default, and a temporary box whose constructor chain passes the limit is no longer removed.** At JDK 25's default `MaxInlineLevel=15` a frame at depth d inlines when d is at most 16. The prelude's `+` reaches `Object.<init>` under its result's box at depth 12, a top-level binding at 10. With the limit lowered to 8, a loop of two nested helper calls rose from 33 to 96 bytes per iteration, since its temporaries' chains no longer inlined. So an operator called from more than 4 further inlined frames keeps its temporary boxes. By reading, the one library's `ZZ32` springboard chain is two classes longer than the prelude's, `ZZ32`, `AnyIntegral`, `Number`, `AnyAdditiveGroup`, `Object`, `Any` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:763`, `:661`, `:380`, `:356`) against `ZZ32`, `Number`, `Object`, `Any` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:210`), since a springboard extends the springboard of its trait's first `extends` entry (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5401-5408`). If `FZZ32` extends the one library's springboard after the switch-over, the margin is 2 frames; not measured, since nothing compiles against the one library yet. Observed once (F-301). Detail: `perf-probes/helper-calls/REPORT.md` sections 3 and 4.
## The checker and the one library

- F-32 **The compiled path cannot reuse walk's glue classes, the Java classes that 28 of the one library's 402 live native bindings still name.** A native binding is a library body `builtinPrimitive("…")`; its string names a glue class, which takes walk's boxed values, or a static helper of `nativeHelpers/`, over plain Java values, which both paths call (F-298; F-299 holds the 374 that name one, and the 28 by type). Matched against those helpers at `a1f8c4b8b`, before any binding moved, the 449 were: 154 whose operation the compiler's prelude already binds to a helper at the same owner and signature, so only the binding's string changes, to name that helper (P-58); 59 whose helper exists, but no binding names it under that name and signature, 23 of them under a name that the compiler's prelude gives to another helper, such as the 12 wrapping operators (row 348); 158 that need a new helper; and 78 that need more, 36 methods of native I/O objects and 42 with no compiled analogue. Of the 449, 29 were object `IntLiteral`'s (`FortressBuiltin.fss:549-629` at `a1f8c4b8b`), 4 among the 154 and 25 among the 158; its 8 conversions and comparisons were then Fortress text over its `asZZ`. Its other 21, and `FloatLiteral`'s 3, left the one library with the two objects, whose place the numeral types `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral` take (F-79; row 578). `println` writes through `stdOut`, a plain Fortress `Writer` over `JavaBufferedWriter`, whose natives name `fileOps` helpers (F-330). - F-54 **The gate classes the distance to the switch-over by root cause.** The `#class` rows of a gate's `distance.txt` hold the count of each class that occurs, such as X1 for an export error, BR for a big operator's body, and OT for the other body errors, one-off library slips and checker limits; `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/classify.py` assigns them, and at a distance of 0 there are none (`tools/distance/table.py:112`). F-53 gives the last gate's total. That gate's `distance.txt` reads '#crash none': the checker checks `value object Char` to its end (F-334), and the `FortressLibrary` component to its end too (F-233). Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage.md` section 2; `reviews/batch-28-review.md`, section 1.
- F-55 **Static arguments are inferred with coercion on both paths: the compiled checker from the arguments' static types and the expected type, walk from their run-time types.** So a mixed-width call takes the narrowest type into which its arguments convert, as P-74 decides. F-73 gives the checker's rule and F-137 walk's; F-87 lists where the checker has an expected type. Under walk, a typed binding converts a call's result after the call and does not fix the call's static arguments: `a: BoxK[\ZZ64\] = wrapK(3)` infers `T` from `3` as `ZZ32` and is refused, since no coercion converts a `BoxK[\ZZ32\]` (row 510). A parameter with no written bound is bounded by `Any` on both paths, so a parameter that nothing fixes takes `Any` (F-78). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferCoercionShapes` and `tests/InferCoercionRungK`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 9.
- F-56 **The compiled checker keeps the expected type, for inferring the call's static arguments, at a call written `f(x)`, which the parser builds as a tight juxtaposition: `f` and `(x)` with no space between.** It keeps it at a method call and an operator too; F-87 lists the other contexts. Only desugarings reach the `fnApp = true` path of `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala:88-90`, so an edit of that path alone changes nothing for a call written `f(x)`. Gated by `compiler_tests/InferCoercionShapes`. Detail: `reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/measure-D.md` section 1.
- F-57 **A numeral's type depends on the path and on the library in scope, and in generic code only the getters `x.zero` and `x.one` and the witness `typecase` give a `T` on both paths.** The witness `typecase` is a `typecase` over a function of type `() -> T`, with one clause for each number type (P-78). The checker types a numeral by its form, `IntLiteral` or `FloatLiteral` under the compiler's prelude and `NaturalNumeral` or `RadixPointNumeral` under the one library (F-79), and converts it into its default where nothing fixes a type (F-342). Walk gives an integer numeral where nothing fixes a type its default by its magnitude, a `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ`, which it prints by those names, and converts it where its place fixes a type (F-341). In code generic over `T extends Integral[\T\]`, `x + 1` fails the checker but runs under walk: no coercion from a numeral into an arbitrary such `T` can be declared, since a generic coercion is refused as a cyclic hierarchy. The checker refuses a numeral outside a bounded number type's range, or rounding to an infinity, statically, and walk refuses an integer numeral out of range when it runs, at the place it does not fit (F-342, F-341). Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage.md` section 2.3; `reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` sections 3.1, 4.1 and 6.2, measured before the numeral switch (F-79); `x.zero` by reading, not measured.
- F-58 **When measured, on an earlier library, microGPT's flat program, C4, had 26 errors of its own under the compiled checker, and none came from a numeral's type.** 15 were arrays without sizes: `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` where the library wants `Vector`, `Matrix` or `Array3`. 5 were numeral powers such as `10.0^(-5)`, refused as ambiguous because two declarations of `^` each needed the integer converted (row 533). 6 were small slips. On a copy patched with decision D's diff, which sizes the model's arrays (P-87), 14 remained: the 5 powers, 3 `DOT` calls that failed on the api's unused sizes, 1 bridge, `adam`'s, that passes arrays sized only at run time, and 5 small slips. Since then the 17 vector and matrix operators' unused sizes are gone (F-35), so by reading the 3 `DOT` refusals are cleared. Since then too, `MultiplicativeRing`'s `^` takes an `AnyIntegral` exponent, and `RR64` declares `^(self, b:AnyIntegral)` beside its `^(self, b:Number)`, the component's header (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:285`, `:367-368`). The distance stage's driver checks a component of `10.0^(-5)` and `10.0^(-8)` against the interpreter's library with no error, so the tie row 533 names does not reproduce there. Each count is a floor, since the checker stops a block at its first failing statement (row 474). Detail: `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 2; `compile-ladder/rung-integer-power/REPORT.md` section 7; `compile-ladder/rung-export-last/SKEPTIC.md` section 3.
- F-59 **`SUM` and `PROD` take their identity from the static argument, and the compiled checker needs that argument written in every clause form.** It builds P-78, with a witness `typecase`, a `typecase` over a `() -> T` function with one clause for each number type. The compiled checker takes the element type from neither the clauses nor a declared type that receives the value (row 731; P-78). So for a generic big operator whose bound names its parameter, such as `SUM`, `PROD`, `BIG MAX` and `BIG MIN`, an unwritten static argument has no instance at its bound, and the call is refused. A plain-bounded big operator takes its bound, or the reduction's expected type where the bound does not fit (F-221). Walk runs such a call: it instantiates the big operator at its value's declared type, else at its elements' join, and leaves the parameter open only with neither (F-228, F-143). C4 writes the static argument, as the team's tests do: `SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#i] matCount(j)`; so does the interpreter's library at its own sites (F-285). `SUM e` over a collection `e`, and `x DOT y`, need none (P-78). Gated, for the witness and a plain bound, by `compiler_tests/WitnessIdentityRungG` and `InferBigOperatorUnwritten`; the refusal is row 731's, and no test pins it. Detail: `reviews/sum-replacement-judgement.md` section 5, Table 2, measured before P-48; row 731 gives today's mechanism.
- F-60 **The coercions between number types carry a sum's zero and a product's one into every wider type by themselves, but not a maximum's identity.** A coercion keeps the arithmetic, on both paths. A maximum's identity is its type's least element, which a coercion does not carry; `ZZ` and `QQ` have none. The library's generic `BIG MAX` and `BIG MIN` have no identity, so an empty one raises `EmptyReduction`. `tests/simpleSum` asserts it for `BIG MIN`; an empty `BIG MAX` raised under walk when measured (`reviews/flattening-questions-ways.md`, "Question 1", section 2). A reduction makes its identity at its own type (P-78). Detail: `reviews/max-min-identities-judgement.md` sections 1 and 2.
- F-61 **`perf-probes/prelude/REPORT.md` named three steps to making the interpreter's library the compiler's: the checker's sizes and the tower's errors are done.** The steps are: the checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters (F-67); the library api's errors from the number and comparison tower are cleared (F-131); and the native bindings move to the compiled path's helpers (F-32). The report's run stopped in the library's apis, before the component, desugaring and code generation (section 5). The component's errors since are the distance, which also had to reach zero before the switch-over, and is 0 since climb batch 22 (F-53). No minimal `Array` or `Vector` added to the compiler's prelude can serve C4's `FlatArrays` (`run-c4/src/FlatArrays.fss`), which extends the library's array hierarchy and uses its whole protocol. Such a shim would reproduce `NativeArray.fss` and about 1,000 lines of the library above it. Detail: the same report, sections 5 (the steps) and 4 (the shim).
- F-62 **The tower closure, `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause, checks as written on the compiled checker, under the specification's reading of `comprises`.** It builds P-44. The checker admits the unlisted `Integral[\I\]` by F-72's rule, which the specification states (F-171); the frozen 1.0 draft refuses it. Walk does not read the library's `comprises` clauses (rows 595, 596). The compiler library's `comprises I` idiom passes the checker and overflows walk's exclusion test (row 407). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-comprises-checker/REPORT.md` section 4.
- F-63 **The one library's api declares `String`'s `split` and `splitWithOffsets` once, abstract; redeclares no `zip` in `List`, where the inherited `ZeroIndexed.zip` serves; has `Condition.map` return `Condition[\G\]`, the component's type; and closes `QQ` by `comprises { ... }`.** `Condition` is the sequential generator trait at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1008`. In their earlier forms, the pair declared twice and `List`'s `zip[\F\](other: List[\F\])`, the checker refused the api (measured). The other repairs tried, the plain pair kept once and a `zip` narrowed to `ZeroIndexed`, read the same count; the forms kept follow the specification's export rules (the report's Decisions). The `Condition.map` error was seen only under a checker change that did not land; otherwise it is read from the export check's comparison of return types, and no test gates that edit. `QQ`'s clause lists no type, since its one value type `Ratio` is private to the component, and an api may leave out a private type only by `...` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:398`). No api-declared type extends `QQ`, so F-64's refusal, which falls on such a type, does not arise. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-defects/REPORT.md`, "Summary", "Decisions" and "Defects and their homes".
- F-64 **The compiled checker refuses every type that an api declares, trait or object, that extends a trait whose `comprises` clause has `...`, whether the clause lists it or not (row 354, open).** So the form `comprises { T, ... }` cannot stand in an api that declares `T`. The refusal runs only when the checker checks an api, so a component's types may extend such a trait. The specification's text allows `...` in an api's clause, and an extender that the clause lists (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, "Trait Declarations"). Only a draft note refuses the api's own declaration of an extender, and a release build leaves draft notes out. The team's `compiler_tests/XXX3q` and `XXX10p` pin the refusal, so a fix that skips it for a listed type turns them red. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-defects/REPORT.md`, "Defects and their homes".
- F-65 **The checker memoizes `TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `excludesClause` per trait table, and the memo changes no answer.** `FORTRESS_ANALYZER_CLAUSES_CACHE=false` turns it off. By reading, both functions depend only on the table and the type. - F-236 **Every method of the build is within HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit but twelve, and a misc-track test fails when that changes.** `MethodSizeJUTest` reads every class of `ProjectFortress/build` with `java.lang.classfile`; it fails on an unlisted method past the limit and on a listed one gone from the build or back under it, and each entry of its list carries its size and what runs it. The twelve: `NodeReader.readNode`, the three parsers' `pCharLiteralContent$1`, `ExprDisambiguator.walk`, `Misc.checkExprMisc`, `HygienicRenamer.walk` (nothing constructs a `HygienicRenamer`), `MagicNumbers.<clinit>` and four `DirectedRoundingTestData` data methods that no suite runs. `WalkerJUTest` still guards `Walker` (F-231). - F-237 **The well-formedness walk reports an ill-formed type whose span lies outside the expression that the walk is in at that expression, so a call whose static argument breaks the bound of the callee's result type is reported at the call.** A call's type keeps the spans of the callee's declared type. An error on such a type is reported at the innermost expression the walk met it in, once for each call that made the type: the expressions that a call's value flows to share its type node and add no error, and a second call with the same printed static argument gets its own error. One known gap, still open (row 776): of two nested calls of one callee at static arguments that print alike, `next[\T\](next[\T\](x))`, only the inner call is reported; the program is still refused. Where the type is ill-formed where it is written, its error stays at the declaration. A local variable's right-hand side is walked before the lines that use the variable, so a call whose value a variable holds is reported at the call, not at a later use. In the library, by reading, reporting at the call adds and drops no error against reporting at the declaration, and the distance holds no well-formedness error (F-53). Source: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TypeWellFormedChecker.scala`, `check`, `error`, `outside` and `within`, and its `SLocalVarDecl` case. Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXStaticArgBoundAtCall`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallOnce`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtEachCall`, `XXXStaticArgBoundAtCallNotAtUse` and `XXXIllFormedTypeAtDeclarationOnce`, and `XXXStaticArgBoundNestedCall`, which pins row 776's single error. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-checker-abstract-callsite/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6, its `SKEPTIC.md` sections 5.1 and 5.2 and its `JUDGE.md`.
- F-240 **The checker's count stage takes about 125 s and its distance stage 224 s at the last landed gate, climb batch 29's.** At climb batch 15b's gate they took 325 s and 1,075 s; the solver's memos (F-235) make most of the difference, not load. Its rise from about 90 s at climb batch 21b's gate is the `FortressLibrary` component's check now run to its end, past its cleared type errors into the export check, not load: rung runs that stopped at those errors took 91 s and 99 s, runs past them 149 s and 151 s, one run each. Since climb batch 21b the checker checks every symbolic operator (F-281), which costs the count stage about 15 to 25 % by its rung's timings of its base and its head in one session. From climb batch 22's gate to climb batch 26's it stayed between about 150 s and 180 s. The count table records no seconds, so its time is the file times of the gate's log; the distance stage (`FortressLibrary` 141 s), over fourteen components, ran at a start load of 0.07, against 205 s (135 s) at 3.42 at climb batch 28's. Both stages about halved at climb batch 27's gate, and no run measured why: each gate ran each stage once, and neither the emptied `Number` (F-324) nor the distance's check stopped at `Char` (F-54) is shown to be the cause. Load can lengthen a stage more than twofold: climb batch 16's merged code took 217 s for the distance stage at its gate, at a load average of 3.3, and nearly the same code took 574 s at 4.6 to 5.3. So a time compares only with one taken under a like load. Source: the file times of the gate's log and `compile-ladder/climb-batch-29/gate/distance.txt`. Detail: `reviews/batch-27-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-26-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-25-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-24-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-23-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-22c-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-22-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-21b-review.md`, section 2; `reviews/batch-17-review.md`, section 1; `reviews/batch-16-review.md`, section 2.
- F-242 **`SUM`'s fusion pairs with `MAX` and `MIN` hold no site of the distance: a `where` condition on each of `SumReduction`'s two `distribute` overloads clears their four unmet bounds, and `ActualReduction`'s generic `distribute`, which `SumReduction` inherits, with its result over its own `K`, clears their two return-type errors.** The fusion pairs are `MaxSumReductionPair`, `MinSumReductionPair` and those two overloads, through which the team's `Generator2` computes the maximum or the minimum of sums in one pass. The two errors were at the two overloads, which answer a pair over `Maybe[\T\]` beside the inherited `distribute`. With the inherited one answering `PossibleReductionPair[\K\]`, they pass the return-type rule (F-75). The team's commented text, which answers `PossibleReductionPair[\R\]`, only moves the two errors to the generic. The fusion stays (P-151). Row 433, fixed; F-250 gives the landing and its test. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` A.1 and A.2.1; `perf-probes/generic-distribute/REPORT.md` sections 3 and 4.
- F-243 **The 13 errors that were filed as waiting on `where` clauses, 13 of the distance's 49 at the gates of climb batches 15b and 16, are all cleared; the 13th, the list comparisons' site, by conditional extension.** The where-clauses probe traced each of them (A.1). The method condition and the generic `distribute` clear the fusion pairs' 6 (F-242). `AnyList`'s `comprises { List[\E\] } where [\E\]` clause, a comment of the team's made live, clears its 4, with its bodies respelled within `AnyList` and none moved into `List` (F-251). A `cast` at `additiveIdentity`'s and `multiplicativeIdentity`'s fallbacks, `else => 0` and `else => 1`, clears 2 (row 436). Conditional extension cleared the list comparisons' site (the list half of row 634; its tuple half was built earlier), with `ZeroIndexed[\E\]` and an element-wise `=` kept outside the condition (F-255). By the probe, library edits with no new language would also have cleared 12: dropping the fusion pairs, moving `AnyList`'s bodies into `List`, and the `cast` at the fallbacks. - F-244 **The three `where` forms that the checker builds (P-151: conditional extension, a function's or a method's condition, and `AnyList`'s `comprises` clause) hold where the where-clauses probe tested them; of the probe's two holes, one stands: a member checked under a conditional extension's condition stays callable where the condition fails (row 773; F-255).** A type variable opened from a `comprises` clause passes the probe's escape, two-value and Amin–Tate tests: the opened type is refused where another type is declared, two values get two types, and Amin and Tate's unsound shape is refused (F-251). The other hole is closed: a method's constraint on its trait's parameter bounds that parameter inside the method and is checked at a dotted call (row 748; F-256). Swift, Rust and Haskell scope such a member to the condition (B.3), which P-151 holds as still to build. The opening of a `comprises` clause has two other open rows of the gap ledger in the checker, 751 and 752; a third, row 775, a crash on such a trait's override, is fixed (F-281). F-250 (row 470) and F-256 give the constraints that the checker does not yet read. Detail: `perf-probes/where-clauses/REPORT.md` B.1 to B.3 and B.6.
- F-245 **With every symbolic operator checked for overloading, the compiled checker finds 5 errors in the library on climb batch 21's first run's code, the distance's 5, where that batch's base gave 191.** The checker checks every operator (F-281), so the distance stage is this check; it gave these 5 with no crash, and gives 0 since climb batch 22 cleared them (F-53). The 191 were measured by the full-check stage, a copy of the checker with every operator admitted that caught crashes per name (`perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/run-shadow.sh`), whose edits no longer match the tree; on climb batch 21's first run's code it caught the `AnyList` crash on `||` (row 809, fixed). Of the base's 186 errors beyond the 5, the library's known fixes clear 54 (F-276), the index bound 124 (F-278, P-156) and the exclusion test 8 (F-277, P-157); measured together on the merged tree, nothing comes. Walk's meet check skips symbolic operators (row 611); widened the same way at `d212b2c1f`, it refused only `EmptyString`'s `||` (F-142). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-symbolic-check/REPORT.md` section 5; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-21/RECORD.md`, "The tests on the merged tree"; `reviews/batch-21-review.md`, section 1; `perf-probes/symbolic-operators-2/REPORT.md` sections 0 to 2; `perf-probes/symbolic-operators/REPORT.md` section 1.5.
- F-250 **Inside a declaration, the compiled checker reads a `where` clause's trait constraint `X extends B` as a bound of `X`, and it adds a constraint on the declaration's own static parameter to that parameter's bound in the declaration's arrow (its function type), so a call is checked against it.** So a method's condition on its trait's or object's static parameter bounds that parameter in the method's body (`compiler_tests/WhereBoundMethodChecker`), and a call that breaks a function's own constraint is refused (`compiler_tests/XXXWhereBoundFunctionCall`, which refuses `g("s")`). A hole remains: a static argument written at a top-level call is not checked against that bound, so `g[\String\]("s")` is accepted (row 470). F-256 holds where the checker reads the constraints at a dotted call, at a type's use and at a `comprises` clause, with its other limits. The library edits that landed with this reading are F-242's (the generic `distribute`, and the `where` conditions on `SumReduction`'s `distribute` overloads for `MAX` and `MIN`) and F-85's (`additiveIdentity`'s and `multiplicativeIdentity`'s fallbacks written `cast[\T\](0)` and `cast[\T\](1)`, and `embiggen` typed `BigReduction[\T,T\]`). Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-distribute/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-251 **A type `where`-clause variable of a `comprises` clause is opened at a call, as a size is, and `AnyList`'s clause, `comprises { List[\E\] } where [\E\]`, once a comment, is in the library.** To open a variable is to give it a fresh type of its own for the call, as the compiled checker already does for a listed type's `nat` and `int` sizes (F-146). So the checker gives an argument whose trait lists `Box[\E\] where [\E\]` a fresh type for the call, bounded by the bound of the clause's binding, `[\E extends B\]`, and by the clause's constraints on it (F-256). It refuses that type in a place whose declared type is another type, and it gives two values two types. It also refuses the shape of Amin and Tate's 2016 unsoundness example, where such a value would prove a subtype relation that does not hold. It does not open such a trait where it reaches it as a parent (row 752). Walk binds the variable as a symbolic type at load. On the rung's own tree the distance went from 49 to 45, row 636's four sites: `AnyList`'s `||` is now accepted through the opened type, and its `addLeft`, `addRight` and the list comprehension's unwrap were respelled. The count, and walk's element types, did not change. Tests: `compiler_tests/OpenTypeChecker`, `XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker`, `XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker` and `XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker`; `tests/OpenTypeWalk` and `AnyListElementTypeWalk`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-anylist-comprises/REPORT.md`.
- F-254 **In the compiled checker, a function or method that leaves out its return type takes it from the one declaration of the exported api whose parameter types are the function's own.** `ApiTypeExtractor` compares the parameter types as the export check does (`ExportChecker.equalTypes`), and a parameter that the function leaves untyped matches any type. It takes the return type only if exactly one api declaration of the name matches. With none or several, it takes none, and the declaration is left as written. So the choice does not depend on the JVM's identity-hash order of the declarations, and no output of the count or distance stage is known to move with that order (F-232): the error at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:130` (`BIG LEXICO`'s omitted return type), which came and went with that order, is gone from both stages. Evidence: read in `scala_src/typechecker/ApiTypeExtractor.scala:77-126` and `:193-209`. Tests: `compiler_tests/OmittedReturnTypeFromApi`, `OmittedMethodReturnTypeFromApi`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-four-rows/REPORT.md`, sections 1 and 5.
- F-255 **The compiled checker reads conditional extension in its subtype relation: a trait or object that extends a type under a `where` clause that binds no variable and holds trait constraints only is a subtype of that type exactly where the constraints hold.** The `extends` entry itself, an object's value parameters and every member are checked with the constraints holding. The static parameters, the declaration's own `where` clause, its `excludes` and `comprises` clauses and its other `extends` entries are checked without them. The disambiguator drops every trait's and object's `throws` clause and contract, so these are not checked at all (row 781). A clause that binds a variable, or that holds a constraint that is not a trait constraint, is read as before: as a parent at every instance. Limits: a member checked under the condition stays callable where the condition fails (row 773), and walk and the compiled run time read the extension at every instance (row 774). Other readers of the `extends` clause in the checker ignore the condition. Those that go through the type's parents see a conditional parent at no instance: the ancestors (`TypeAnalyzer.ancestors`), which the overloading checker reads to let a concrete method implement an abstract one. Those that read the clause itself see it at every instance: the inherited `excludes` clauses (`TypeAnalyzer.excludesClause`). None of these readers moved a result on the library, and no ledger row holds them (report section 10). In the library, `List` extends `LexicographicOrder[\List[\E\],E\]` only where `E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\]`; its `ZeroIndexed[\E\]` entry and its own element-wise `opr =` stand outside the condition, so every list keeps them (`Library/List.fss:106-107`, `:124-128`). On the rung's own tree, against climb batch 17's gate, this cleared the distance's site of `LexicographicOrder`'s `a CMP b` over an unbounded `E`, in `FortressLibrary.fss`, and added none. Tests: `compiler_tests/CondExtendChecker`, `XXXCondExtendRefuseChecker`, `XXXCondExtendUnconditionalEntryChecker`, `XXXCondExtendExcludesChecker`, `XXXCondExtendComprisesChecker`, `XXXCondExtendParamBoundChecker`, `XXXCondExtendExcludesWhereChecker`, `CondExtendInheritedMember` (a type that inherits through a conditional parent compiles: the code generator's analyzer reads the parent at every instance), `tests/XXXConditionalExtensionTypeTestWalk`. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-checker-conditional-extension/REPORT.md`, sections 1, 6 and 10.
- F-256 **The compiled checker checks a `where` clause's trait constraints where they apply.** At a dotted call, a candidate whose `where` clause constrains its trait's or object's static parameter is not applicable where the receiver's static argument breaks the constraint ('Method Holder[\String\].showIt is not applicable: its where clause requires String to extend Shows.'). If a function's or method's `where` clause has a trait constraint, the clause's `nat` and `int` variables become static parameters of its arrow, inferred at the call. So a constraint whose bound names such a variable is met where some value of it meets every constraint. When the type variables' solutions leave only size constraints, the solver tries once more to solve them. Walk and the compiled path both refuse a function's or method's type `where`-clause variable at name binding ('E is undefined.'), so this inference never reaches one. A trait's or object's own constraint is checked where its type is used, with the bound's message, also at a constructor call through the call's type. A type `where`-clause variable of a `comprises` clause is bounded by its binding and by the clause's constraints on it, where it is opened and in the check of an extender. In a bound that names the variable itself, as `E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\]` does, the opened type stands for the variable. - F-97 **The ladder-regression stage's baseline is `compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`.** The gate compiles and runs the files of its `pass-list.txt`, and compiles only the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, which its `microgpt-phase.md` holds at the phase disambiguate. - F-98 **The harness's `run_out_WIcontains` key is whitespace-insensitive containment.** It collapses runs of whitespace in both the output and the expected string, where `_WImatches` collapses them in the output only. A key that `generalTestFailed` does not know sets no check, so a misspelt key checks nothing. A `run_out` with no check falls to the default: the output contains `pass` or `PASS`. Source: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:155-188`, `:276-282`.
- F-99 **The gate's thread count is pinned in the build file for the two suites, not in the calling shell.** `build.xml`'s `fastTrack` macro, which runs `testFast`, and its `systemShard` macro, which runs `testSystem`, set `FORTRESS_THREADS=4` (P-125). Without the pin, the suites would take the caller's count: half the CPUs if it is unset, or 1 under `env.sh` (F-203). `fastTrack` also pins `JAVA_FLAGS` to `-Xmx4g -Xss64m`, because a compiled test's run step takes its heap and stacks from it. With `JAVA_FLAGS` unset, a compiled test's run step (`bin/run`) gives its threads the JVM's default 1 MB stacks, and at four threads `library_tests/TimingRungT` overflowed in 8 of 12 runs (row 640). The rule does not reach these open defects: a static argument that only the call's result mentions, at a typed binding (row 510); and a varargs or tuple parameter over mixed widths (row 511). Nor does it reach, by inference and not measured, a numeral that fits `ZZ32` passed alone for a parameter whose bound a `ZZ32` neither extends nor coerces into, since walk reads such a numeral as a `ZZ32` (P-76). Gated by `tests/InferCoercionRungK.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 9.
208	- F-138 **Each integer type declares its own `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX`, so under `walk` the family answers at the type that its arguments promote to.** It builds P-47. Each type also declares its own `MAXNUM` and `MINNUM`. Under walk an `NN32` operator with a numeral answers an `NN32`, the numeral converting into `NN32` (`tests/NumeralWithNN32.fss`). Compiled, `NN32` with `ZZ32` or `ZZ64` answers `ZZ` (row 442). Gated by `tests/IntegerMinMaxRungM.fss` and `IntegerMaxNumMinNum.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-integer-minmax/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 9.
209	- F-139 **`RR32` is a sibling of `RR64` under `Number`, and `RR64` converts from it.** Nothing converts into `RR32`. Under `walk` two `RR32`s answer an `RR32`, and an `RR32` with an `RR64`, a float numeral or a `ZZ32` answers an `RR64`. A typed binding converts an `RR32`, but a declared return does not (row 387). On the compiled path the prelude's `RR32` has no `=` (row 528), and two `RR32`s answer an `RR64` (row 529). Gated by `tests/RR32SiblingRungV.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-rr32-sibling/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 11.
210	- F-140 **A size beyond `NN32` or `ZZ32` is refused by the compiled checker when it is a literal or folded from literals, and by walk when it binds one; walk reads a size exactly.** It builds P-40. The checker refuses such a size outside its kind: 0 to 4294967295 for `nat`, and `ZZ32`'s range for `int`. Walk refuses it at run time, where it binds the size to a static parameter. Walk reads and computes a size exactly, with no wrap: it reads a size used as a value as a `ZZ32` up to 2^31-1 and as a `ZZ64` above. The checker types such a value `ZZ32` (P-173, F-342). The compiled class loader checks no size that it computes at instantiation: `next[\nat k\]()`, which builds a `Box[\k + 1\]`, answers 4294967296 at `k = 4294967295` (gap-ledger row 675; F-222). Gated by `tests/NatBigSizeWalk` for walk's reading. The refusals are gated by `compiler_tests/XXXNatRangeChecker`, `XXXNatArithRangeChecker` and `NatRtBigSize`, and by `tests/XXXNatBeyondNN32Walk`, `XXXIntBeyondZZ32Walk`, `XXXIntBelowZZ32Walk`, `XXXNatArithProductWalk` and `XXXNatArithSumWalk`; each `XXX` test passes because its program is refused. Open under walk: an array of a static size from 2^31 to 2^32-1 stops at its store's factory, 'Closure/Constructor for makeJavaArrayStore parameter 1 (n:ZZ32) got type Long', where no catch sees it (row 527). Also open (row 962, contested): a `nat` or `int` size of 2^31 or more read as a value raises a `java.lang.Error` on the compiled path that no `catch` sees, and is a `ZZ64` under walk, where P-173 makes it a `ZZ32` and no decision says where such a size is refused; under walk a `ZZ32`-declared return passes such a size on as a `ZZ64`. 211	- F-141 **Under `walk`, a type parameter that nothing at a call fixes takes its declared bound, and a lone one with no narrowest candidate takes its bound where every argument is below it.** It builds P-48. A lone type parameter is one that is the whole declared type of some argument and that no other argument fixes (F-137); where some argument is not below its bound, it takes the arguments' join. A type parameter that the declared parameter types mention only in function domains, an odd number of arrows deep and never inside a static argument, as `T` in `g: T -> ZZ32`, is bounded by the arguments only from above. Where nothing bounds it from below, it takes the meet of its declared bound and the bounds that the arguments place on it. An F-bounded parameter stays open (F-143). First, a parameter that only another fixed parameter's bound mentions takes that parameter's instance, not its own bound: `ap[\T, A extends T\](a: A)` gives `T` the type of `a` (D3, row 592). Second, a lone one whose bound mentions a static parameter has the arguments' supertypes among its candidates, and so takes their narrowest common supertype, never its bound (D5). 214	- F-144 **The identity-less reductions are typed at their element type: `AssociativeReduction[\R\]` lifts to `Maybe[\R\]`, and its `simpleJoin` and every `lift` take `R`.** A reduction that extends `AssociativeReduction` declares `simpleJoin` at its element type; walk refuses one at `Any` at load. One with static parameters escapes that check and stops at its first join (row 665). A static argument that names the lifted type, as in `generate[\Maybe[\R\]\](...)`, is `Maybe[\R\]`: with `AnyMaybe`, the non-generic trait that `Maybe` extends, the program stops under walk. With the element type unwritten, `BIG MINMAX` and the four tuple forms `BIG MIN_MIN`, `BIG MIN_MAX`, `BIG MAX_MIN` and `BIG MAX_MAX` run under walk. A plain-bounded monoid operator with no static argument is instantiated as F-228 says. So `List`'s `BIG CONCAT` runs, also over a list of list comprehensions. `BIG SQCUP` and `BIG SQCAP` ran in one measurement each, with no gated test, and `PrefixSet`'s `BIG UNION` and `PureList`'s `BIG CONCAT` were not measured. Gated by `tests/UnwrittenBigMinMaxWalk`, `UnwrittenTupleMinMaxWalk`, `UnwrittenBigOperatorsWalk`, `UnwrittenComprehensionElementsWalk` (`List`'s `BIG CONCAT`) and `ReductionSimpleJoinAtAnyWalk` (the refusal at `Any`). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-reduction-types/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 8; `compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md` section 7 (the operators that ran).
215	- F-145 **Walk refuses at load an object that leaves an inherited abstract method uncovered.** Bodies at narrower parameter types define an abstract method only where together they cover its parameter types, with `comprises` clauses read, as P-147 decides: each position is split through the clauses, and every combination of parts must lie inside one body. A search that does not settle refuses the object: a cycle, a symbolic type or a type that the search cannot read, 10,000 steps or 4,096 combinations. A generic object is not checked (row 665). An object whose one covering definition has a static parameter of its own is refused, though it is valid (row 728, a defect of walk; the compiled path runs it). The compiled checker covers the same way, within the same bounds, except that where the abstract method or a body below it has static parameters of its own, it does not split the parameter types, so it refuses an object whose cover needs a split (row 725). Walk's `override` check at load is F-147's, and its check of the Meet Rule for Functional Methods is F-142's. Gated by `tests/AbstractMethod*Walk` (`AbstractMethodCoverUnsettledWalk` among them) and `compiler_tests/AbstractMethodCoveredPairs`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-coverage/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6 (the cover); `compile-ladder/rung-duplicates-coverage/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 8 (the refusal of a search that does not settle).
216	- F-146 **The compiled checker accepts arithmetic in a size, and compares two sizes by their written form once it has computed each operation on numerals.** It builds P-55, the curator's decision on arithmetic in a size. Two sizes are the same where their written forms match once each operation on numerals is computed. They differ only where they are two different numerals or two different size parameters, so the checker calls a `typecase` clause unreachable that walk reaches at equal arguments (row 683, contested). Any other pair, such as a size name against a numeral, or two operations written differently, is not known to differ. Neither path infers a static parameter that a parameter type writes inside an operation (row 767). The compiled class loader can make a size outside its kind's range, as a `nat` above 4294967295, where walk refuses it (row 675). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatArith*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-expressions/REPORT.md` section 1, "Item 15, 15a with its part (b)", and section 12.
217	- F-147 **Walk refuses an `override` that overrides nothing; an inherited declaration is overridden where each of its parameter types, not counting the self parameter, is a subtype of the `override`'s and not all are equal.** This is the traits chapter's "strict subtype" (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:585-589`). At an instance of a generic trait that an object without static parameters extends, equal parameter types still count as overridden (`OverrideGenericInstanceEqualTypesWalk`). Walk checks the `override` of a generic trait, object or object expression once, at its declaration. An object inherits nothing that a trait's `override` overrides, so an object below an abstract `override` that declares no body is refused at load (rows 614, 649; `AbstractOverrideUndefinedWalk`, "does not define an abstract method declared in type W"). Walk does not read all the bounds of the static parameters in an object expression, which takes them from the function around it, or in a generic trait or object that extends a type under a `where` clause. There it accepts an `override` over an inherited declaration whose parameter types mention a static parameter and differ from the `override`'s (row 693). The `fortress-repo` skill gives the rule's cases (`references/interpreter.md`, "What walk checks"). Gated by `tests/Override*Walk.fss` and `AbstractOverrideUndefinedWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-override/REPORT.md` section 1.
218	- F-148 **Under walk, a `where` clause's bound on a static parameter bounds that parameter alone.** The bound goes into an extends list of the parameter's own. Every unbounded static parameter of a load shares the top type's one list, so a bound written there would bound them all. Gated by `tests/WhereBoundOverloadWalk.fss` and `OverrideAfterWhereBoundWalk.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-override/SKEPTIC.md` section 3.
219	- F-222 **Walk computes a power in a size exactly, as the compiled path does, and refuses a negative exponent.** A negative exponent can come only from a static parameter. A power beyond its parameter's kind is refused at binding, as any size is (F-140). The compiled class loader checks no size it computes against its kind, and stops on a negative exponent with a Java exception (row 675). Gated by `tests/NatArithPowerWalk` and `NatPower*Walk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-popl-examples/REPORT.md` sections 3 and 6.
220	- F-228 **Under walk, a reduction or a comprehension that writes no static argument instantiates its big operator by a declared type, else by the join of its elements' run-time types, else at its bound, where an F-bounded parameter stays open.** It builds P-48. The declared type is a local variable's, or a top-level or local function's declared return type, for either also where the clause form ends a block. A method's return type, a top-level variable, a field, an assignment, a function expression, a branch, a call's argument and another clause form's body do not direct it. Otherwise the clauses run once into the library's collector, `__elemsOf`, which keeps the elements in order, typed at the join of their run-time types, and the operator is instantiated at that join; the reduction then runs over the collected elements, so each body runs once. A declared type or a join that does not fit falls back to the instance that no hint gives: a plain-bounded parameter takes its bound, and an F-bounded one stays open (F-143). So a `SUM` of `ZZ32` and `RR64` values, whose join `Number` is outside the bound, runs with each `+` at its operands' types. The same holds with no element and no declared type. With the big operator so instantiated, the library types `__bigOperator`'s local function `body(i: I)` at the element type `I`. A big operator whose declared result is a trait of its own is read through the `BigReduction`, `Comprehension` or `BigOperator` that the trait extends (row 718, fixed). Still wrong, each a ledger row: an empty clause form that no declared type directs takes its bound or stays open (row 716); a comprehension that no declared type reaches is built at the join of its elements' run-time types, which a declared `List[\Shape\]` refuses where its elements are all `Circle`s (row 717); a clause form that is a call's argument gets no declared type (rows 510, 705). Gated by `tests/UnwrittenListMapComprehensionWalk`, `UnwrittenComprehension*Walk`, `ComprehensionTypedBindingWalk`, `UnwrittenSetBigOperatorsWalk`, `UnwrittenEmptyFloatSumWalk`, `IntMapComprehensionTypedWalk` and `UserBigOperatorResultTraitWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md` sections 1, 5 (5.3 lists the contexts) and 10, decision 6; `compile-ladder/rung-walk-overload-if/REPORT.md` section 1, "Row 718".

- F-114 **`ant testSpecData` runs 130 of the specification's 133 extracted examples under walk, as a gate step, and all 130 pass.** `SpecDataJUTest` runs `SpecData/examples/basic`, `preliminaries` and `advanced`, not `library/`'s three, and `testFast` excludes it. It builds P-124. Five examples write no static argument on a generic big operator whose bound mentions its static parameter, and they pass only because walk leaves that parameter open (F-143; row 424, fixed). The count and the time: the last landed gate's `summary.txt`.
- F-203 **`explorations/experiment/env.sh` sets up a shell for the gate's runners, and sets `FORTRESS_HOME` from its own place in the tree.** It sets `FORTRESS_HOME` two folders above itself, replacing any value that the shell had (`env.sh:4`), so sourcing another tree's `env.sh` runs that tree's code. It also sets the JDK, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` and `JAVA_FLAGS`, and unsets `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`. It deletes a `/tmp/fortress*rats` parser folder only if nothing in it was written for an hour and every running `java` process started after its last write, so sourcing it does not break a live run. The compile ladder's drivers source it: `compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh` and its copy in `baseline-2026-09-19/`, and the two that the gate's ladder regression runs, `repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh` and `baseline-2026-09-19/microgpt-phase.sh`. Each of these sets its own `JAVA_FLAGS` after it. `experiment/setup.sh` sources it too. `microgpt-phase.sh` names the main tree's `env.sh` by its absolute path; the gate rewrites that path in its copy (the `fortress-repo` skill's `gate.md`, "The ladder regression"). The count stage's and the distance stage's `run.sh` do not source it: their headers tell the caller to source it first. A worker does not source it. It starts each Bash call with the `fortress-repo` skill's setup lines, which give the same settings (`build-and-caches.md`, "Setting up each call"). Evidence: read in the scripts; the deletion rule also in `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/build-efficiency.md` section 4.
- F-234 **A Fortress command that a worker types itself (`bin/fortress`, `harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh`, or `java` of a Fortress main class) starts a fresh JVM, and that start costs too little to pay for a resident compiler.** A resident compiler is a background JVM that serves Fortress commands, as Scala 2's `fsc` did. The suites start one JVM for each test class, and one for each of `testSystem`'s four shards, not one for each test: the harness runs each test file inside its JVM. Only a compiled test's run step and a `.sh` test, such as `tests/concurrentPrinting.sh`, start another process. In one measurement over 267 worker transcripts, the one-off commands took 17.5 % of the wall time of the workers' shell commands, and the suites, builds and stages 47.8 %. Over the workers' whole running time, the one-off commands took 6.4 % (11.6 % if every wait that the measurement could not tie to a run was theirs). Removing their JVM start-up would save at most 1.8 % (P-150: no resident compiler is built). What runs inside the suites and the stages was not measured. Detail: `coordinator/process-engineering/fresh-jvm-commands.md`, "Summary", "What a resident compiler could save, at most" and "Decisions not taken".
- F-283 **The 52 programs of the team's `DemoTests` reach their end under walk.** Run one at a time from `ProjectFortress/demos`, each exits 0 and prints no "fail", within a 600 s limit and on an empty input, with `wordcount2` run from the tree's root and `tennisRanking` given the three files of `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:806-815`. The demos run in no suite, so a batch that changes walk or its library runs them again (P-79). `Generator2Demo` draws its arrays by `random`, so a product of them can overflow in `PROD`, and one such `IntegerOverflow` stop in a run is not a regression. The compiled checker still refuses `trips.fss` (row 817). No gated test: the command is the driver in `compile-ladder/rung-team-demos/REPORT.md` section 13, and its output on the code that `4445d848b` committed is 'demos: 52 run, 52 reached their end'. Detail: the same report, section 3; `compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/REPAIR-review.md`, section 2.
- F-295 **The distance stage counts each api's own errors and crashes, so an error in an api that only a later target checks cannot hide.** `table.py` turns `#total` into `none:` for an api whose `@@TC API` line gives `errors=` above 0 and that printed no `@@SC` line of its own, naming it with its count, and turns an `@@TC API-CRASH` line into a `#crash` row of kind `api` (`explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/table.py:54`, `:61-67`, `:94-104`). It does not read the `@@TC COMPONENT-CRASH` lines that `tools/distance/shadow-patch.py:111-113` prints. Test: `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/test_classify.py`, `Readings`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-list-imports/REPORT.md`, sections 1 and 2.
## Landed semantics

- F-117 **A compiled mutable variable's cell holds the language's top type, so a mutable variable of arrow type compiles and runs.** The cell holds `fortress.AnyType.Any`, not `FValue`, because a compiled closure is not an `FValue`. The cell's gated tests, `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevel*Var` and `MutableTopLevelVarInLoop`, run no variable of arrow type. Detail: `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 4.
- F-118 **A numeral's value reaches the compiled world intact, and the compiled path prints a large `NN32` or `NN64` value unsigned, but it cannot compare a numeral beyond `ZZ64` with another numeral.** The code generator carries a numeral of its own type as an `int`, a `long` or its decimal string, by its exact bit length, and a numeral that the coercion desugarer types at a library number type as that type's constant (F-340). So on the compiled path `4294967295` and `18446744073709551615` keep their values, as walk does at `ZZ` and `ZZ64` (walk converts a numeral bound to `NN32` or `NN64`, F-341). The compiled path prints an `NN32` or `NN64` value above its type's signed half unsigned (F-313; test `compiler_tests/UnsignedPrintingCompiled`). It compares two `IntLiteral` values at `ZZ64`, so `lt(18446744073709551615, 5)` for `lt(a: IntLiteral, b: IntLiteral): Boolean = a < b` fails with `Not in range for ZZ64` (row 328), which no test pins; an untyped binding of such a numeral is a `ZZ`, its default (F-342). An `IntLiteral` arithmetic result of 64 bits or more also keeps its value compiled: observed in the report's probe, and no test gates it. Walk stops the same program at `x + x` with `IntegerOverflow`, since its fixed-width addition raises (F-132). Gated, for the numerals at `ZZ`, `ZZ64`, `NN32` and `NN64`, by `compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2`. Detail: `compile-ladder/repair-r2-literal-wrap/REPORT.md`, "The failure-mode question".
- F-119 **The library's scalar extension is eight generic declarations: `+`, `-`, `MIN` and `MAX` between an `Array[\T,I\]` and a scalar `T`, in both orders.** `T` is bounded by `Number` and `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` for `+` and `-`, by `Number` and `StandardMin[\T\]` for `MIN`, and by `Number` and `StandardMax[\T\]` for `MAX`. Gated by `tests/ArrayScalarExtension.fss` and `tests/ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary.fss`. The second imports the fixture `test_library/ArrayOperatorVocabulary`, which declares two overloads each of `MINMAX`, `+` and juxtaposition over the library's arrays. Walk checks such overloads against the library's only on a cold cache (F-269). So a pass of that test shows that they coexist with the library only if the run started from an empty cache. Detail: `reviews/library-scalar-extension-review.md`, change 1.
- F-120 **A top-level variable imported through an api can be read, assigned and read back on the compiled path.** The checker asks the declaring api whether the name is mutable, and the code generator binds a mutable one to its cell. Gated by `compiler_tests/ExportVarRungX.test`, and the refusal to assign an immutable one by `XXXExportVarRungXFrozen.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-export-var/REPORT.md`, "What the rung landed".
- F-121 **The team's spelling of `AnyIntegral`'s `comprises` clause, `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]`, stays a comment, and no decision says whether it is a valid clause.** The live clause, which lists `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `ZZ`, `NN32` and `NN64`, stands (P-44), and the compiled checker accepts it (F-62). The specification lets a listed type hold a `where`-clause variable, at every value of it, and the compiled checker opens such variables, of a `nat`, an `int` or a type (F-146, F-251). As the team wrote it, the clause is ill-formed: past the front end's refusal of such a clause on a trait that declares a coercion (row 831), the compiled checker reports 'Ill-formed type: Integral[\I\] The static argument I does not satisfy the corresponding bound Integral[\I\]', since `where [\I\]` binds `I` without the bound that `Integral[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` asks for. With the bound, `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` in place of the list, the checker finds 0 errors in every api of the one library, but the `FortressLibrary` component's overloading and export checks run out of memory at the stages' 4 GB heap (`TypeAnalyzer.ancestors`, `TypeAnalyzer.scala:1023`) and finish clean at 11 GB ('#total 0', '#crash none'). Neither can be reached on `main`, where the clause is not live; no test checks either, and the probe's lifter fix and clause are at the end of its report. Of the team's commented `comprises ... where` clauses, P-151 builds only `AnyList`'s. The comment stays by P-44, which kept it beside the live clause when its `where` form was not built. Whether it becomes live now that the checker opens such variables is an open question, whose default leaves it. Detail: `coordinator/process-engineering/facts-slice-2.md`, "Points for the checker", point 1; `perf-probes/anyintegral-comprises-where/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5.
- F-122 **`round` on an `RR64` or an `RR32` sends an exact half to the even integer on both paths.** NaN gives 0, and a value beyond the `ZZ64` range saturates to the `ZZ64` bounds. On both paths, a numeral within half an ulp of a tie is rounded as its nearest double, not as the rational that it denotes, against the specification (row 360). The ties are gated under walk by `tests/RoundHalfEvenRungR.fss`, and on the compiled path, for `RR64`, by `library_tests/RR64FunctionsRungF.fss`; the compiled `RR32` ties were observed in a probe of the report. NaN and saturation are gated on neither path: they were observed in the report's walk probe and compiled differential, and read in the code (`(long) Math.rint` in `Float.java:384`, `RR32.java:326` and `simpleDoubleArith.java:132-134`). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-round-half-even/REPORT.md`, "What landed" and "Differentials".
